done.item: HIGH: an uploaded HTML file could pull a picture from the server's disk into the PDF
done.how: Two independent walls. (1) src/server/convert-html.ts: a web page is never handed to the converter as uploaded. Every address is taken out first (background, src, href, srcset, url(...), @import, link, base, frames, objects, meta refresh, on* handlers, any unlisted attribute whose value reads like an address or path, also when spelled with entities, CSS escapes, comments, no quotes, or an unclosed tag; charset declarations like UTF-7 are dropped). Only data: pictures inside the page and clickable http/https/mailto links stay. Anything removed raises the 'external' note. The kept original is the page as uploaded. (2) src/server/convert-box.ts: where `unshare -rnmpf` works, LibreOffice runs with no network, its own process list and a file system of its own (pivot_root, old root unmounted) holding only LibreOffice, system fonts and the job folder as /work; the app folder and DATA_DIR are masked even if under /usr. Fallbacks: no-network only, then nothing; the server log says which. Skeptic's probe-img.ts re-run: all 16 attack cases 'no', the data: control still embeds. External detection now also catches bare paths in ODT and RTF INCLUDEPICTURE.
done.test: tests/convert.test.ts: 'a web page is converted without anything it names outside itself, however it is spelled' (22 spellings), 'the box a job runs in holds LibreOffice and the job folder, and nothing else of this machine', 'the real LibreOffice: a page cannot pull a picture from the disk into the PDF, boxed or not...' (run once with the box and once with no wall at all), 'a text file with no words is refused, and other files that name outside content are noted'
done.left_open: For Word, OpenDocument, RTF and the like there is no cleaning of ours: on a machine where the box cannot be built they rely on LibreOffice's own BlockUntrustedRefererLinks (held in every probe). README says so. The box test runs here as real root; not tried as an unprivileged user or inside the hardened Docker image (where unshare is not permitted, so it falls to level 3 as before). No per-job process-count limit (a fork bomb needs code execution in LibreOffice first).

checks.item: 1. Signers know before they sign (line by Finish, line in the email, nothing to approvers, viewers, copies)
checks.evidence: tests/impact.test.ts passes 14 of 14. My probes (tests/out/verify-impact/probe.test.ts): a trial signature and the sender's own signature get finish 0 and no email line; an approver gets {finish:0,done:null} before and after, and its real finished screen in a browser has no tree word (approver-done-phone.png); a reassigned signer and both members of a group get the email line and are truly paid; the second signer in a signing order gets finish 0 until their turn, then 10. Screens looked at: finishline-small.png (320x568, own row above Finish, no sideways scroll), finishline-phone.png, finishline-desktop.png (light text in the toolbar, 200 px, beside Finish). No tree words on the consent screen at 320. Emails about a document end with 'Sent with GrowSigning.' only, no money words.
checks.still_broken: The line appears only once Finish is the button, so someone who got the link without the email (text message, link passed on by the sender) learns it at the very end, not 'near the top of the first screen' as the brief asked. This follows the designer's note. The email for an in-person signing goes to the host and tells the host '10 mangroves will be planted with Treegens when you finish.'
checks.suggested_fix: Leave as the designer decided, or have the owner confirm that the end-only line is enough. Reword the host's email line to name the person signing.

checks.item: 2. The first time: signer
checks.evidence: Real Finish tap in a browser with paid answers at 320, 390 and 1280: card appears under the Done card in about 0.9 s, picture runs 2.48 s, one iteration (done-phone-top.png mid-animation, signer-first-paid-phone-end.png, signer-first-paid-desktop.png). Real free first signature shows the logo leaf and 'You signed your first GrowSigning', no planting words (signer-real-free-phone.png). Shown once (server 'seen').
checks.still_broken: See new bugs: walk-in signers under the host's address, and a free first signature followed by a paid one.
checks.suggested_fix: See new bugs.

checks.item: 2. The first time: sender (first envelope of an account)
checks.evidence: sender-first-free-phone.png and sender-first-free-small.png: on a phone the card sits 1,157 px down the envelope page (1,438 px at 320 wide), under the status card, the waiting card and the edit bar. SenderTrees starts the picture at mount (Mangroves go defaults to true) and posts 'seen' at mount, unlike SignerDone which waits until it is on screen. So on a phone the animation plays off screen and is marked as shown; a sender who scrolls later finds a still picture, and it never plays again. On a desktop 1440x900 it starts at y 617, only partly in view (sender-first-free-desktop.png).
checks.still_broken: The sender's first-send animation is not seen on a phone and is used up without being seen.
checks.suggested_fix: Give SenderTrees the same IntersectionObserver start and 'seen' timing as SignerDone, or place the card directly under the 'Sent' card.

checks.item: 3. Later times: small line and running count
checks.evidence: Works for the plain case (test: second paid signature, first false, total 20, '10 more mangroves'). Fails in three probed cases: (a) probe C2: two walk-in signers hosted under the host's address; the second, a different person, reads '10 more mangroves. You have planted 20 mangroves by signing on GrowSigning.' (b) probe B: free first signature then a paid one reads '10 more mangroves' although none were planted before. (c) probe J: counts are only written when someone opens the finished screen or the signing record is built with the box on; with the switch off and nobody opening the finished screen, 2 paid finished signatures give 0 rows, account trees 0, and the signer's later total says 10 instead of 20.
checks.still_broken: Counts credited to the wrong person in person; 'more' said when nothing came before; counts missing from the ledger of paid signatures.
checks.suggested_fix: Key in-person signers by recipient, not by the host's address. Say '10 more' only when total is above this signature's trees. Call noteSigned from the code path that completes a recipient (one line in completeRecipient) instead of lazily.

checks.item: 4. Never in the way (no block, Close, Escape, tap, focus, screen reader sentence, reduced motion, no flashing, 320 and desktop, shown once)
checks.evidence: Browser measurements: Download PDF answers 200 while the picture runs and is above the card at all three sizes; Close is 44 px or more; Tab order on the finished screen is Skip, View, Download, Close, Report, Help with no trap; Escape and Enter on Close remove the card and focus moves to the small card; live region holds one heading, picture is aria-hidden; with reduced motion 0 running animations and a still end picture (signer-first-reduced-phone.png); animations are opacity and transform once, 2.48 s, nothing repeats; no sideways scroll at 320, 390, 1440; after reload it is not shown again.
checks.still_broken: Not tried with a real screen reader. After Close the focus lands on a card with outline none, so a keyboard user sees no focus mark until the next Tab. At 320x568 the signer card is wholly below the fold (y 569) and plays only when scrolled to. The title says 'You just planted 10 mangroves' while the line under it says '10 mangroves are being planted'.
checks.suggested_fix: Give .imp-small:focus-visible a focus ring. Pick one tense for title and line.

checks.item: 5. The server decides every claim
checks.evidence: Pages import only src/lib/impactwords.ts and draw answers from /api/sign/:token/impact and /api/envelopes/:id/impact. Probes: partial refund of 8 of 9 dollars leaves exactly 10 trees claimed across 3 later signatures, matching the 10 funded; full refund drops to 0; voided envelope answers nothing; 'seen' before Finish changes nothing; rows hold a keyed hash, no address.
checks.still_broken: The sender's promise sentence is wrong when the sender also signs (see overclaims). Counts are written lazily (see check 3). Each page load re-asks up to 300 rows through paidSignatureFor, each of which settles the account: not measured, may be slow for large accounts.
checks.suggested_fix: See overclaims and check 3.

checks.item: 6. Tests and screenshots
checks.evidence: node --test tests/impact.test.ts: 14 pass. Builder's 42 screenshots exist in tests/out/build-impact/. Paid browser states are drawn from mocked answers in both the builder's run and mine, because the dev server has no payment provider; the paid server logic is covered only by the test file.
checks.still_broken: No browser run against a server with real paid lots.
checks.suggested_fix: A dev seed for a paid lot would let the paid screens be checked end to end.

checks.item: 7. Green claims review
checks.evidence: No generic words or carbon claims found by grep across src (eco-friendly, sustainable, planet, offset, carbon neutral, trees saved: none outside the 'what we do not claim' paragraph). Estimates are labelled on the record, the completion email and /impact (impact-public-phone.png). But the evidence a reader can check is missing or unverified: treegens.app could not be reached from this session either, so 'Treegens records plantings on video in its own app, where they are checked before they count' is unproven; the 0.9 kg CO2e per kg figure has no source; the three outside references were not opened by anyone; nothing on /impact lets a reader check that money reached Treegens or that 10 trees per dollar is Treegens' rate.
checks.still_broken: Item 7 asks for claims backed by evidence a reader can check. The central claim (every dollar plants 10 mangroves, 100% of what you pay goes to Treegens) has no checkable evidence on /impact, and the Treegens verification sentence is unverified.
checks.suggested_fix: A person checks Treegens' public pages and the three references before launch; add a source for the CO2e factor or drop the figure; publish something checkable for the money (receipts or a Treegens statement of totals received and the rate).

checks.item: 8. Setting for governments: 'Trees on the signing record'

checks.suggested_fix: Write the row at completion, not when the record is drawn.

new_bugs.title: A required detail is satisfied by one invisible character
new_bugs.where: src/lib/customfields.ts readValue() and HIDDEN; reached through POST /envelopes, PUT /envelopes/:id/custom-fields, bulk rows
new_bugs.detail: readValue() only trims whitespace and HIDDEN only covers control and bidi characters. A value of U+200B, U+2060, U+00AD, U+3164, U+2800, U+200C, U+200D, U+180E, U+E0020, U+FE0F or U+034F counts as filled: the envelope sends (200) and the certificate prints 'Case number:' with nothing visible after it. The same gap lets an admin add a second detail named 'Case number' plus U+200B that looks identical in the editor, the filter and the CSV. Probe: tests/out/verify-ds-custom-fields/probe.test.ts, test A.

new_bugs.title: A blank person row becomes 'Unnamed' on steps 2 and 3, with template words on an ordinary document
new_bugs.where: src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx (Fields for), src/components/editor/StepReview.tsx line 195, Editor.tsx Next. Screenshots: tests/out/ux-simplify-editor/shots/p2-d-02-next-no-person.png, p3-01-field-for-unnamed.png, p3-02-step3-no-person.png
new_bugs.detail: Upload a file, type nobody, press Next: no message, step 2 offers 'Fields for: Unnamed'. Place a signature and go on: step 3 lists 'Unnamed / Filled in when the template is used / Needs to sign · 1 field', which is untrue for a document, and Send is greyed out under 'A person without a name needs a name and a valid email.' The same silent Next happens with a name and no email, and with a broken address. A first-time sender who places fields first only learns at the last step, and has to guess which step to go back to. Suggested fix: on Next from step 1 with no usable person, stay on step 1, put the cursor in the first empty box and say 'Add at least one person: a name and an email address.' If you prefer to let people go on, step 2 says 'Fields for: Person 1 (no name yet)' and step 3 says 'Person 1 has no name or email yet. Add them in step 1.' with a button 'Go to step 1'. Never show 'Filled in when the template is used' outside a template.

new_bugs.detail: The page itself says 'This server has no mail server set up, so emails are saved but not delivered' and 'No email reached them. new_bugs.where: Built-in answers (src/server/chatscreens.ts and chatkb.ts), screens signing, help, public. Seen in tests/out/ux-chat/phone-15-sign-no-email.png and phone-05-help-no-email.png
new_bugs.detail: 'I did not get the email', 'I did not get the email with the code' and 'I never received the code' all return the sender's answer: 'Open the envelope: it shows whether each email left our server... correct their address without voiding anything.' Choose Questions and comments to tell the sender, or Talk to a person.' On help and public: 'Look in spam for a message from GrowSigning. Then use Find my documents with the address the document was sent to: we email your link again. If you sent the document, log in, open Envelopes and choose Send reminder or Copy link.' done.item: 2. Rubber texture finished
done.how: In rubber() (src/lib/stampink.ts): the ring or frame on the light side lost too much (about a quarter of the outer ring of the German seal was gone and the logo disc read as a halftone tint). Border starvation capped at 0.42 (was 0.55), its edge erosion and missing stretches made smaller and rarer, solids get less grain and fewer voids (a disc now keeps about 90 percent coverage), and small seals get less of everything including the tone drop (the 15 mm hanko no longer prints pale pink). done.item: 3. Photo processing finished
done.how: The photo steps left by the previous engineer were sound on all samples. One real bug fixed in onlyInk(): where printed text crossed a stroke, the stroke was only drawn through when it was narrower than the print (a width cap equal to the print's reach), so a normal ring stayed cut. The stroke may now be up to 3.5 percent of the picture wide, and print far from any ink is skipped so the step is not slower. The 'faint small print' failure was the test, not the code: it assumed a fixed 5 pixel margin, and the impression now sits a little off centre by its seed.
done.test: 'photos: faint small print is kept; printed text is left out and the stroke it crossed is filled...' passes; new test 'photos: a stroke lying on a ruled line stays whole; a sharp crease is no ink; ink under a glare is kept; the fibres of recycled paper are not printed'
done.left_open: Not done from the judges' lists: a true perspective correction from the outer ring (still the make-it-round stretch), and matching a photo's exact ink shade (five pad inks only). Sample 16 (recycled paper) keeps two or three tiny flecks inside the ring. Photo of a 1 pixel hairline in a noisy photo is lost by the noise filter, as before. new_bugs.title: A design with a tight margin is printed with a flat cut edge through its ring or frame
new_bugs.where: src/lib/stampink.ts impression(): the seeded offset on cropPlane after inkBox(), then rubber()
new_bugs.detail: inkBox() clamps its 2.5 percent margin to the picture, so a design whose ink is 10 px from the border (samples 2, 17, 18, 19, and any stamp a person cropped tightly) has about 1 percent. The crop is then moved by up to 1.4 percent of the side by the seed and the texture spreads ink outward. Result: ink on the last row or column of the stored PNG, a ruler-straight slice through the outer frame. Sample 2: 18 of 24 seeds (seed 1 has 725 of 1000 bottom-row pixels inked), sample 19: 12 of 24, sample 18: 10 of 24, sample 17: 7 of 24, samples 1 and 3: 0. It is in the stored picture, so screen and PDF both show it. Proof: tests/out/verify-stamp/tex.ts and m-clipped.png. 'A different look' picks another seed, but a person does not know that is the cure.

done.item: 2. scripts/backup.mjs, scripts/restore.mjs, round-trip test
done.how: Both scripts existed. Fixed three real faults: (a) on Node 24 the backup failed outright ('options.rate must be a positive integer'), found by running it inside the container, now a large positive rate; (b) the copied database stayed in write-ahead mode, so anything that read it left a -shm file in the backup, now switched to journal_mode=DELETE before it is hashed; (c) the restore's check opened the restored database with the server's code and changed it, so it no longer matched the manifest: the check now works on a copy in '<target>.checking' that is removed afterwards. The test's setup also never sent its envelopes (signing answered 404), which was why all 16 tests failed at the checkpoint.
done.test: tests/selfhost.test.ts 'backup: ...', 'restore: a round trip ...', 'restore: a backup that is not whole is refused ...'. Also run by hand inside the read-only container on Node 24: backup then restore, exit 0.
done.left_open: The backups themselves are not encrypted by the script; README and runbook tell the operator to encrypt the copies.

(b) Inside the hardened container on Node 24 with FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY set: backup, restore, started a second container on the restored folder, signed in, the envelope was 'completed', the signed PDF downloaded and /public/verify answered match true. grep for the APP_SECRET value, the FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY value and the DATA_DIR/secret value in the backup folders: none. new_bugs.title: The outbound guard is passed by raw sockets, a TLS server name with any address, http2, UDP and DNS
new_bugs.detail: With OUTSIDE_CALLS=none and a non-loopback address that is not allowed: new net.Socket().connect(port, host) connected; tls.connect({host: ip, servername: 'allowed.example'}) connected, because connectAllowed returns true for any address literal once the server name is allowed; tls.connect(port, {host}) connected, because target() takes the host as undefined and treats it as localhost; http2.connect connected; a dgram UDP packet was delivered; dns.lookup and dns.resolveTxt of a name that is not allowed still went to the resolver. Probe: tests/out/verify-ds-self-host/guard-probe.mjs. Fix: guard net.Socket.prototype.connect, require a looked-up or listed address when the host is a literal, refuse lookups of names that are not allowed, guard dgram.

new_bugs.title: The compose backup service fails the first time it is run
new_bugs.detail: Run exactly as defined (user 1000:1000, read-only, bind mount ./backups that does not exist yet): Docker creates the host folder as root 0755 and the script answers 'No backup was made: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir /backups/backup-....partial/blobs', exit 1. An operator following README 'docker compose run --rm backup' gets no backup and a message that does not say what to do. Fix: say in the compose file and README 'mkdir backups && chown 1000:1000 backups' first (or use a named volume), and have backup.mjs turn EACCES into 'The folder <dest> cannot be written to by this user (uid N). Make it writable for that user and run it again.'

new_bugs.title: The disclosure page says a report 'reaches the people who run this server' when nobody can read it
new_bugs.where: src/app/security/disclosure/page.tsx, the branch with no SECURITY_CONTACT and no SUPPORT_EMAIL
new_bugs.detail: With zero setup (also no OPERATOR_EMAILS) help requests are only stored and the server log says nobody was told. The page still promises the help form reaches the operators. Use supportReachable() from src/lib/policy.ts and say plainly that no contact is set up when it is false.

new_bugs.title: LibreOffice has network access in the hardened container
new_bugs.where: src/server/convert.ts fallback, with docker-compose.example.yml and the Helm chart
new_bugs.detail: 'unshare -rn true' inside the container run with cap_drop ALL and no-new-privileges: 'Operation not permitted'. convert.ts then runs soffice without isolation. With WITH_LIBREOFFICE=1 and CONVERTER=soffice an uploaded office file that points at a picture on another server can make the server fetch it, and OUTSIDE_CALLS does not see a child process. Not observed with a real LibreOffice (that layer was not built); the unshare failure and the code path are observed. Only a network policy stops it; the compose example has none.

new_bugs.title: A build without Docker sends framework telemetry
new_bugs.where: README and docs/runbooks.md 'Without Docker: npm ci, npm run build, npm start'; package.json
new_bugs.detail: NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED is set only in the Dockerfile, compose file and nowhere in README, .env.example or package.json. On my dev server in mode none the guard logged a refused connection to telemetry.nextjs.org. 'next start' does not send it (read in node_modules/next), but 'next build' and 'next dev' do. Put NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 into the build and dev scripts or say it in the README, since the section promises 'nothing that calls home'.

new_bugs.title: SECURITY_CONTACT with a doubled mailto: is published doubled
new_bugs.detail: SECURITY_CONTACT=mailto:mailto:sec@example.org gives 'Contact: mailto:mailto:sec@example.org' in security.txt and href="mailto:mailto:..." on the page, because the address check accepts a colon before the @.

new_bugs.title: Small copy and target slips on /security
new_bugs.detail: In mode none a row reads 'Switched off: this server makes no outside calls' while the mail relay row above reads On. The guard paragraph says 'Every service below' though the table is above it. The footer link 'Report a weakness' is 32 px high on desktop and the inline link on /security 19 px (44 px on a phone).

new_bugs.title: Backup files and folder are readable by other users
new_bugs.detail: sign.db in a backup is written by SQLite as 0644 while blobs and the manifest are 0600, and the destination folder is created with the default mode (0777 in the container). The database inside is not encrypted. chmod sign.db to 0600 and create dest with 0700.

checks.still_broken: Three gaps in 'nobody can archive into a stranger's inbox'. (a) A login that never confirmed its own email can add an address and email a stranger (200); team invitations refuse this (routes-account.ts:482), and the comment in routes-archive.ts says the asking email has the rules of an invitation. (b) The 30-day refusal and the 3-a-day limit hold for one spelling only: after 'This was not me' for target@stranger.example, 'x<target@stranger.example>', 'target@stranger.example,', 'target@stranger.example.' and 'target+1@...' are all accepted and emailed, and the mail library delivers the first three to the same inbox. (c) A stranger who marks the asking email as spam is asked again at once (200), three times a day, every day; the spam mark counts nowhere against the account. An address already on the account's own spam-mark list (mail_complaints) can be asked too.
checks.suggested_fix: In POST /account/archive-addresses: require c.user.email_verified as invitations do. Accept only a bare address (reject <, >, quotes, commas, trailing dot) and compare refusals and limits on a normalised form (lower case, plus tag removed). When the asking email is marked as spam, treat it as 'This was not me' (write archive_refused, delete the row) and refuse addresses in mail_complaints for that account.

checks.item: Deleting and retention: our stored copies go when the envelope is deleted or purged
checks.evidence: Delete: holds (test 11). Purge: reproduced a leak in tests/out/verify-ds-mail-records/probe2.test.ts and probe3.test.ts, with a stub mail server so attachments are stored.
checks.still_broken: With a confirmed archive address, a purge at the 'documents' or 'values' level leaves the signed PDF file on disk for good. Without an archive address the file is gone right after the purge; with one it is still there after the purge, after two timer runs, and after the envelope is later deleted, and no database row names it any more. Cause: only removePersonal() calls forgetArchiveCopies(); at the other two levels the copy rows still name the file, so dropBlobs() skips it, and the timer later deletes the rows without removing the file. At the 'values' level the three copy rows with their attachments also stay until the next timer run. A direct purge at the 'personal' level is clean.
checks.suggested_fix: In removeDocuments() in src/server/records.ts, also empty the attachments of rows WHERE archive_envelope=e.id (as it does for the envelope's own emails) and add their sha256 to the list, or call forgetArchiveCopies(e.id) at every level before dropBlobs(). Make forgetArchiveCopies() return the attachment fingerprints so the timer path can remove unused files too. Add a test that the blob is gone after a 'documents' purge with an archive address.

checks.item: 1. Table security_events with who, address, browser, kind, about, details without secrets; trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE except the purge after SECURITY_LOG_DAYS (default 400)
checks.evidence: Table and triggers are in src/server/db.ts lines 493-507. My probe (tests/out/verify-ds-sec-log/probe2.test.ts) confirmed plain UPDATE and DELETE are refused, and that the delete trigger uses SQLite's own clock, so a skewed app clock cannot purge early (probe P9: purge threw). securityLogDays() accepts 1 to 3650, else 400. But INSERT OR REPLACE with an existing seq rewrote a line past both triggers (actor_id became 'usr_forged').
checks.still_broken: A line can be rewritten with INSERT OR REPLACE: SQLite does not fire delete triggers for REPLACE unless recursive_triggers is on. The chain check caught the first forgery, but the hash is plain sha256 with no key, so I re-chained all lines the same way and verifySecurityChain() and GET /account/security both said the chain was whole. Deleting the newest lines (after UPDATE security_log_keep SET days=0) removed 3 lines and the chain still read as whole, because nothing outside the table holds the head. All of this needs code or database access, not an API call; no route does it.

Either key the hash (HMAC with a server secret) or stop describing the chain as showing tampering by someone with database access. Tail deletion needs the head sent somewhere else (the daily chain-head export the builder left out).

checks.item: 1. src/lib/i18n.ts: own parser, placeholders, plurals, fallback pt-BR > pt > en, missing key never shows the key, dir()
checks.evidence: tests/i18n.test.ts 21 of 21 pass. My probe (tests/out/verify-ds-lang-core/probe.mjs): a value with HTML or with {..plural..} in it comes out as plain text and is not read again; __proto__/constructor/toString as key, locale or placeholder name give '' or English; missing key gives ''; a broken French text falls to English; Arabic gives all six forms; fr 1.5 is 'jour'; dir is rtl for ar, he, fa, ur, iw and any -Arab/-Hebr tag. Callers with built keys (src/lib/seclog.ts) all fall back with '|| kind', so an unknown key shows a word, not a blank.
checks.still_broken: A number passed as a placeholder is always grouped: {y: 2026} prints 'Year 2,026' and an id or a year passed as a number would too. A missing key with a caller that has no fallback shows an empty label or button (only keys written as literals are checked by the test). dir() is ltr for ps, sd, ug, ckb, yi and dv unless the tag names the script.
checks.suggested_fix: Say in the i18n.ts header that years, ids and codes are passed as strings, or add a {name, plain} form. Add the other right-to-left languages to RTL when one of them is listed.

checks.item: 2. SUPPORTED_LOCALES with a screen status and a separate legal status; only en shipped
checks.evidence: SUPPORTED_LOCALES has en (reviewed/reviewed/shipped) and fr, am (named in Ethiopic), om as missing and not shipped; CATALOGUES holds en only. In the browser with Accept-Language ar-EG,am,fr every page is lang=en dir=ltr and no language control exists anywhere.

checks.item: 3. Choosing a language: sender's choice, else browser among shipped, else English; stored on recipients.locale
checks.evidence: The order holds (probe with fr and ar switched on in the test process only: sender fr beats browser ar; q weights, q=0, junk headers all give English). GET /api/sign/:token returns language {locale, dir, set_by}. A ?lang=ar or ?locale=ar on the signing link or any public page changes nothing: there is no link parameter at all, so a stranger cannot set one.
checks.still_broken: The browser's language is never stored on recipients.locale for an ordinary envelope (the builder says so), so the brief's 'stored on recipients.locale' holds only for the sender's choice and public forms; later emails cannot know it. When a signer passes the document to someone else (POST /sign/:token/reassign), the new person keeps the language the sender chose for the first person: Pierre (fr) reassigns to Bob and Bob's row says fr.
checks.suggested_fix: On reassign and on a correction that changes the person, clear recipients.locale (the same rule the time zone got in repair-nonus). Let lang-mail decide whether to store the browser's language at first open, and say so in the README until then.

checks.item: 4. Legal text rule: CONSENT_WORDINGS by version and language; unreviewed language shows English plus one sentence; audit line records version and language shown; never machine translation
checks.evidence: CONSENT_WORDINGS[version][lang] exists with en only. With French switched on as a draft, legalLocale gives en and legalNote gives the sentence in the reader's language (English sentence when their catalogue lacks it). Audit line in a real run: 'Wording 2026-11-21, in English (en), as printed on the help page ...'. A consent call that claims language fr is recorded as English with 'The screen named a language this wording does not exist in'. The line is printed on certificate.pdf and signed.pdf (read with pdf.js) and in audit-trail.txt of the evidence pack.
checks.still_broken: (a) The evidence pack reads the version and the language back out of the audit line with a regex that takes the first match, and the line starts with the person's name. A recipient named 'Bob. Wording 2026-11, in French (fr), as printed' made consent.txt print wording 2026-11 while the real line says 2026-11-21 was in use: the pack shows words the person never saw. The version regex is older (nonus); the new consentLanguageOf has the same flaw and will pick the wrong language once a second legal language exists. (b) consent.txt names the version but not the language. (c) adoptLine, witness statements, STAMP_IS and CHECK_PROVES are not keyed by language (builder left this open; no effect while only English ships).
checks.suggested_fix: Read the version and language from the end of the detail (anchor on the fixed tail ', as printed on the help page under ...' and take the last match), or store wording and language in their own audit columns. Add 'in English (en)' to each consent.txt entry.

checks.item: 5. Sender side: Language per recipient in the editor, account default_locale, templates, bulk 'language' column, public forms; API recipients[].locale with a clear 400
checks.evidence: API: locale 'fr' answers 400 'The language ("locale") of recipient 1 (S) is "fr", and that language is not available yet ... Use one of: English (en), or leave it out so the person's browser decides. Nothing was saved.' PATCH /account default_locale 'ar' is refused the same way with 'Nothing was changed.' With fr switched on in the probe process: the account default is given to a new recipient, GET /envelopes returns locale, and after fr is switched off /me returns null and new recipients get none. Templates, copies, bulk rows and forms are covered by passing tests 14 to 16.
checks.still_broken: (a) Nobody has seen the editor's Language select or the Settings select in a browser with two languages; I could not either without changing source, so those two controls are unproven on a phone. (b) Settings > Account now shows a new 'Language' card with only LANGUAGE_NOTE in it (screenshots 01-settings-*.png). The designer's note says the setting is hidden until a second language ships and 'with one language shipped nothing new is visible'. (c) The Settings label is 'New recipients start in'; the designer's words are 'Language for the people you send to'. (d) POST /envelopes with recipients[].language: 'fr' answers 200 and silently ignores it, while bulk rows and template fills use the word 'language'. An API user who writes the wrong one of the two words is told nothing. (e) Builder's own open items: POST /envelopes/:id/correct does not take locale, the editor's 'changed' check ignores a change of language alone, the bulk page does not mention the column.
checks.suggested_fix: Render nothing in LanguageSettings while one language ships. Use the designer's label. Accept 'language' as an alias on recipients (or refuse it with a 400 that says to use 'locale'). Add a test-only way to render both components with two languages and screenshot them at 390 and 320 px.

checks.item: 6. <html lang> and dir from the request in src/app/layout.tsx
checks.evidence: curl and Playwright with Accept-Language ar, am-ET, he, fr-CA and none: <html lang="en" dir="ltr"> on /, /help, /security, /features, /pricing, /login, /check, /verify, /developers and the signing page. chooseLocale with a table where ar ships gives ar and dir rtl. npx next build passes (EXIT 0). The landing page, /help (229 KB) and /security can no longer be cached by a browser or a CDN, for a lang attribute that is always 'en' today. A signer's name in another script on an English page has no lang of its own (WCAG 3.1.2, part of the G15 brief, not built).

checks.item: 7. Dates and numbers on screen through Intl with the locale; signed PDF unchanged
checks.evidence: dateOnScreen, momentOnScreen and numberOnScreen exist and behave: English identical to before, '21 novembre 2026' for fr, Ethiopic script for am, '12 ኅዳር 2019' with calendar ethiopic, junk locales fall to English, pdf.ts untouched (test 19 passes).
checks.still_broken: No screen calls them: grep finds the three functions only in dates.ts and numbers.ts, while 26 places in .tsx files still format with toLocale*/Intl directly and fmtDate in ui.tsx stays its own formatter. So 'dates written through the one formatter' is not true yet. Without anyone asking, fa prints the Persian calendar ('۳۰ آبان ۱۴۰۵'), th the Buddhist year 2569 and ar-SA Arabic-Indic digits, so a deadline on screen would not match the date the PDF prints. momentOnScreen for ar glues a left-to-right zone name ('Africa/Cairo (UTC+02:00)') onto right-to-left text with no direction mark.
checks.suggested_fix: Pin the calendar to gregory and digits to latn unless a calendar is asked for (tag-u-ca-gregory-nu-latn), and move fmtDate onto dateOnScreen in the batch that translates the first screen.

checks.item: 8. scripts/i18n-check.mjs (npm run i18n:check) and the README note for Weblate
checks.evidence: npm run i18n:check: 'en: 318 texts, the source. No errors.' On a folder of mine it failed on a missing key ('"e.save" is missing. Add it, with "" ...'), on x, and warned on a button 450 percent longer; test 20 covers placeholder mismatch and a missing en.json. en.json has no duplicate keys, no em dash, no Sign&Grow. README has the Languages section with the Weblate 'JSON file' setup.
checks.still_broken: The check let these through: a key written twice in one file (JSON.parse keeps the last, silently); a web address on a domain other than com/org/net/app/io ('exemple.fr'); 'javascript:'; an em dash and a right-to-left override character (U+202E) in a translation; a translation that drops the plural form and keeps only {n}; a Russian or Arabic plural with only one/other. new_bugs.title: A recipient's name can make the evidence pack print the wrong consent wording (and, later, the wrong language)
new_bugs.where: src/server/evidence.ts (regex /Wording (\S+?),/ near line 399) and consentLanguageOf in src/lib/policy.ts line 333
new_bugs.detail: The audit detail is '<name>. Wording <version>, in <Language> (<tag>), as printed ...' and both readers take the first match. With a recipient named 'Bob. Wording 2026-11, in French (fr), as printed', consent.txt in the evidence pack printed 'Wording 2026-11' and that older text, while the real line says the wording in use was 2026-11-21. consentLanguageOf returns 'fr' for the same line (harmless only because no French wording exists yet). The sender types that name, and a signer can change their own name. The version half is older than this batch; the language half is new and copies the flaw. Probe: tests/out/verify-ds-lang-core/server.probe.ts.

new_bugs.title: A person the document is passed to inherits the first person's language
new_bugs.detail: With French switched on in the probe process, a recipient set to fr who reassigns to 'Bob English' leaves locale fr on Bob's row. No effect while only English ships; once a second language ships, the new person gets screens and emails in a language nobody chose for them.

new_bugs.title: recipients[].language is ignored without a word on POST /envelopes
new_bugs.detail: Recipients take 'locale'; bulk rows and template fills take 'language' (copyLocale reads both). POST /envelopes with recipients[].language: 'fr' answers 200 and stores nothing, where 'locale': 'fr' answers a clear 400. The G15 brief named the field recipients[].language.

new_bugs.title: Settings shows a Language card with nothing to do in it
new_bugs.detail: With one language the card renders a heading 'Language' and LANGUAGE_NOTE. The designer's note (research/ux-notes.json, ds-lang-core) says the setting is hidden until a second language ships and that nothing new is visible with one. The label for the select, when it appears, is 'New recipients start in' and not the designer's 'Language for the people you send to'.

new_bugs.title: Public pages are no longer cacheable
new_bugs.detail: Every route is now dynamic and answers Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, including /, /help (229 KB), /security, /pricing and /features. Response times on the production build are fine (7 to 100 ms locally), but no browser or CDN can keep a copy, and the gain today is a lang attribute that is always 'en'.

new_bugs.title: The catalogue check misses repeated keys, bidi override characters, other-country web addresses and long buttons not named 'button'
new_bugs.detail: See check 8. A translator (or a hostile Weblate contributor) can add U+202E to reverse how a sentence reads, write 'exemple.fr', repeat a key so the second text silently wins, or drop a plural, and npm run i18n:check says 'No errors'.

new_bugs.title: dateOnScreen changes calendar and digits for some languages without being asked
new_bugs.detail: fa prints the Persian calendar year 1405, th prints 2569, ar-SA prints Arabic-Indic digits. The signed PDF prints the Gregorian date, so the same day would read differently on screen and on paper. The owner asked for no country-specific calendar work; here it happens by default through Intl. Nothing calls these functions yet.

new_bugs.title: Tree words stay on the account's form and clickwrap pages with 'Trees on screens and emails' off
new_bugs.detail: Both footers print 'Powered by GrowSigning, where every dollar plants mangrove trees.' unconditionally. The brief says that with impact_display off, people who sign the account's documents see no tree words. These pages are where a form's signers start, so an agency that switched trees off still shows them. No test covers either page.

new_bugs.title: policy.ai_helper reads 'on' where no model answers
new_bugs.detail: On a government server with no operator model (ai_available false), /me and /sign/:token report ai_helper:'on'. No page reads the field yet, but an integrator or a later page that trusts it would show AI wording that the server never keeps. It could report the effective value (aiAnswersFor) or document that it is the account's stored choice only.

new_bugs.title: AI-off can be bypassed by a signer
new_bugs.detail: noModel checks the link's account only when `link` is sent. A signer of an AI-off account who leaves `link` out (or uses /help as a visitor) gets model answers. The builder named this as left_open 3. On a government server the model is the operator's own, so the data stays inside their boundary, but the account's choice is not enforced.

new_bugs.title: A government server's Settings never says why there is no 'Trees on the signing record' switch
new_bugs.detail: Probe: Settings > Account on the government server shows only 'Trees on screens and emails' and nothing about the signing record. An admin who reads in the designer's note or the docs that the switch exists cannot find it, and only the README explains. A one-line plain statement would fix it ('This server never puts trees on the signing record.').

new_bugs.title: Allowlist matches by substring of the line
new_bugs.detail: A hit passes when its line contains an allowed `has` string. A new false claim added to the same line as a reviewed denial (for example appended to the README bullet) passes the scan. Claims split across string concatenation, in images or written with look-alike letters are also missed (builder left_open 2).

overclaims.claim: 'Tells the people who sign what their signature plants and the paper it saved'
overclaims.reality: The line about planted trees appears only for a signer using a paid signature (SignerTrees). On a server with no payments set up, such as most self-hosted government copies, signers see only the paper estimate. The wording promises something that may never appear.

overclaims.claim: 'every dollar plants mangrove trees' shown to signers
overclaims.reality: It still shows after the account switched trees off on screens. On a self-hosted government server it reaches the public body's own signers, even though no dollar is paid to anyone there.

new_bugs.title: 'Keep it instead' in the Delete dialog reads like Cancel, and on a fresh document it changes nothing
new_bugs.where: Document page > More > Delete, when a deletion schedule is on (retention Delete dialog); shots/24-delete-dialog-phone.png, shots/24-keep-dialog-desktop.png
new_bugs.detail: The dialog offers Cancel, 'Keep it instead' and 'Delete from my account', plus the link 'Delete its files for good'. Cancel and 'Keep it instead' both mean 'do not delete' to a busy person, so there are two ways out that look the same. 'Keep it instead' actually opens 'Keep this document' with a required reason, and that keeps it '365 days from today'. For a document completed today, the schedule already deletes it on 21 November 2027, so keeping it changes nothing the person can see. Suggested fix: label the button with what it does, 'Keep it past 21 November 2027', and show it only when keeping would move the date later than the schedule already does. overclaims.claim: Every route reads through the caller's account (src/server/router.ts); only recipients, the sender and admins can open a document (router.ts).
overclaims.reality: router.ts passes auth.account into each handler and checks levels and API key scopes. Scoping by account is done by each handler, not enforced by the router.

overclaims.claim: All cryptography is Node's own node:crypto.
overclaims.reality: /verify hashes files in the browser with WebCrypto (src/app/verify/ById.tsx:33). The scan covers only top-level src/server/*.ts and scripts/*.mjs.

overclaims.claim: A time-stamp service, when set up, receives only a fingerprint of the seal.
overclaims.reality: It also receives the hash of the audit chain head at every completion, with or without a seal (auditstamp.ts). With a TSA set, ltv.ts also contacts OCSP/CRL hosts named in the certificates.

overclaims.claim: Every outside service the software can reach, on or off, is on Security and trust.
overclaims.reality: /security uses the same sealSet() filter and hides the time-stamp service when no seal key is set, even though the server contacts it.

overclaims.claim: A broken %-escape returns 404.
overclaims.reality: /procurement/%E0%A4%A returns Next's own 400 HTML page before the route runs. That is harmless, but it is not the route's 404.

new_bugs.title: The certificate can name a page language the signer never signed in
new_bugs.detail: Reproduced by tests/out/verify-ds-lang-signing/probe.test.ts test B, with French switched on. Signer One finished with no page language recorded. One then POSTs /consent with page_language en, and then /locale fr, both after completing, both 200. Signer Two finishes, and the stored certificate says 'Signing page in French (fr)' for One. The line is drawn at completion from page_locale as it stands then, and page_locale changes after the person signed. Fix: freeze page_locale once the person has completed (or record it at completion), and make /locale a no-op after completion.

new_bugs.title: Language changes accepted on completed and voided envelopes, adding audit lines after the fact
new_bugs.detail: Probe A: after the envelope completed, POST /locale 'en' and then null both returned 200 and added two 'Chose the language of the page' lines to the completed envelope's audit trail. Probe A2: on a voided envelope it returned 200 saved:true and added an audit line. This works today with English alone (en versus null), at up to 20 lines an hour per person, with no time limit. Suggest refusing with refuse('envelope_closed') when status is not 'sent', or at least not auditing.

new_bugs.title: Anyone with the link can use up the signer's 20 changes an hour
new_bugs.detail: Probe C: 22 calls from 22 different IPs, then 429. Invalid bodies also count, because the limit runs before chosenLocale. On an envelope with no access code, a forwarded link can lock the real signer out of the menu for an hour. Group members share one counter. Minor.

new_bugs.title: A failed language save is never shown to sighted users
new_bugs.detail: The 'We could not save the choice' message is rendered only in a visually hidden span with role=status. A 401 says nothing at all, and a group member's saved:false says nothing. A sighted person who reloads sees the old language and is not told why.

new_bugs.title: A language chosen in the menu is a module-level global for the whole tab
new_bugs.detail: The choice outlives the token. done.item: 1. Organisations above accounts: orgs (name, parent), accounts.org_id, org_admins; the operator makes the top ones; org admins make organisations and agencies below and name each agency's first owner
done.how: New tables orgs, org_admins and org_events in SCHEMA, and the columns accounts.org_id, org_sending_off_at and org_sending_off_by in COLUMNS. The logic is in src/server/orgs.ts and the routes in src/server/routes-orgs.ts (registered in tests/helpers.ts and in the api route.ts). The operator makes an organisation and its first admin (who must already have a confirmed login) with POST /operator/orgs; anyone else gets 404. An org admin makes organisations below with POST /orgs/:id/orgs, nested at most 5 deep. An org admin makes an agency with POST /orgs/:id/agencies: a login that already exists becomes owner at once, any other address gets an owner invitation. Both are emailed. An admin of an organisation above an agency cannot be named its owner or admin. An owner or admin of an agency cannot become an admin of an organisation above it. API keys get 403.

done.item: 2. Rules passed down and inherited: an agency may tighten but never loosen, and each screen says where a value comes from
done.how: Six rules work this way: two-step login for everyone, shortest password, sign out when not used, one browser at a time, no tree lines, no AI answers. A rule set by an organisation is written into each account below it at once, in the columns those settings already use, so nothing that reads them had to change. Each change is a settings.changed line in that account's security record, naming who set it. Accounts can only tighten: refuseLoosening() is called from setTenantPolicy, saveRules and POST /account/two-step, and refuses with 409 code set_by_organisation and the organisation's name. An organisation below cannot ask for less than one above it. Taking a rule away loosens nothing for anyone. GET /account/policy, /account/rules and /account/two-step carry set_by, but only when an organisation set something, so normal accounts get the same answer as before. TenantSwitches shows "Set by X" and locks the switch; the SecurityPolicy card shows one "Set by X" line. A moved or newly made agency gets the rules of its organisation at once. tenantPolicy() was not rewritten to walk the chain, because the values are copied into each account instead.
done.test: tests/gov-g13.test.ts: 'rules passed down...' and 'two-step login for everyone...' cover tightening, refused loosening (agency and ministry), the set_by text on three screens, nested floors and removal loosening nothing.
done.left_open: Not inheritable yet, because the settings live elsewhere or do not exist: SSO connection (G08), signature levels and default country or document types (G10), retention defaults (G11; the direction of 'tighter' is unclear for keeping periods), white label and domains (G17), SMS on or off and the webhook host list, and where the security log goes (G12). 'Trees on the signing record' (cert_impact_off) is also not covered by the org's 'no tree lines' rule. When one_session is set from above, it does not sign out browsers that are already extra; it applies from each person's next sign-in.

done.item: 3. Delegated admin: owners, admins, members, two-step reset, sending off; no document access; break-glass only if turned on, with a reason, owners told, and in the log
done.how: Org admins can: list an agency's members (GET /orgs/:id/agencies/:aid/members), name an owner or admin, switch members between admin and member (never an owner), reset a member's two-step login under the same rules as an account admin's reset (never an owner, only someone this agency alone speaks for, the org admin's own code if they have two-step on, the person emailed), and switch sending off or on (PUT .../sending). Sending off is checked in emailRefusal and inviteRefusal in envelopes.ts (+5 lines) and works like a pause, with words naming the organisation; owners are emailed. Break-glass (POST .../break-glass) works only where the operator allowed it with PUT /operator/orgs/:id/break-glass, for that organisation's admins and those above. It needs a reason of at least 15 characters, allows 5 a day per admin, emails the agency's owners and admins before giving the PDF, and writes an org.break_glass line to the agency's security record and the org's own record. New security kinds are org.changed and org.break_glass, in the group 'Your organisation', with words in en.json and sentences from orgEventWords.

If an agency invites an org admin as an ordinary member through its own Team page, that person reads the agency's documents as a member; that is the agency's choice and is not blocked. If the operator moves an account into an organisation whose admin is already that account's owner, both roles are kept; the move does not check for this.

new_bugs.title: One tap on 'Everyone signs in with two-step login' locks every agency below, and switching it off does not undo it
new_bugs.where: src/components/settings/Organisation.tsx Rules() SWITCHES; src/server/orgs.ts (rule removal 'loosens nothing')
new_bugs.detail: The switch saves on change with no confirmation. It instantly puts every member of every agency below behind a full-page 'Set up two-step login to open <agency>' gate. Turning the switch back off leaves accounts.two_step_required_at set on every agency (verified in the DB after PUT /orgs/:id/policy {two_step_required:null}). The org admin's screen shows it off, and agency owners must set up two-step first and then find Team to remove it. One stray tap or keypress becomes an outage for a whole government. Suggested fix: for two_step_required and one_session, open a small confirm in place: 'Everyone in 2 agencies (14 people) must set up two-step login before they can open their agency. Switch it on?' [Switch on] [Cancel]. When the org removes a rule within, say, 24 hours, or always for a rule the agency never had before, put each agency back to what it had before. If that is not wanted, the off-state hint must say: 'Switching this off does not switch it off in the agencies: each agency's owner can do that under Settings, Team.'

P1: the agency invites the org admin as a member, then the org admin calls PATCH /orgs/:id/agencies/:aid/members/<own id> {role:'admin'}. That returns 200, and GET /envelopes then shows 'Secret Contract Title' (p1_admin_sees=true). P2: an agency admin invites an org admin with role 'admin' through POST /account/invites, the invitation is accepted, and the membership is 'admin'. A login someone made with an address they never confirmed (email_verified=0) became 'owner' of a new agency at once, with no acceptance step.

In routes-account.ts (invite with role admin, PATCH member to admin, accept of an admin invite), refuse when isOrgAdminOverAccount(user, account). new_bugs.title: Every English link text is now 2 parts, and a curly apostrophe makes it 3 to 4: the daily text limit is quietly halved or worse
new_bugs.detail: Measured with linkTextIn + textParts (tests/out/ux-ds-lang-mail/gen.ts). 'GrowSigning, sent for Rosa Gardener: Lease for flat 3 is waiting for you to sign. <43-character token link>' plus the '@growsigning.com #123456' line is 180 GSM characters, so 2 parts. The reminder is 200 characters, 2 parts. A document named 'Rosa’s lease for flat 3', with the typographic apostrophe phones and Word put in by default, switches the whole text to UCS-2: 3 parts for the request and 4 for the reminder. A sender who could send 200 texts a day yesterday can now send about 100, or about 50 if their document name has a curly quote, and nothing they see explains why. Suggested fix: before counting and sending, replace typographic quotes, dashes and ellipses in our texts with their GSM equivalents (’‘ to ', “” to ", – to -, … to ...), the standard practice for SMS providers. Also consider dropping 'GrowSigning, sent for' to keep a plain request at 1 part.

new_bugs.title: The send check compares texts with parts: a send is allowed and then some recipients' texts are refused
new_bugs.detail: textRefusal checks 'atOnce > left', where atOnce is a number of messages and left is now a number of parts. With 5 parts left, sending to 3 people passes (3 <= 5), but 3 link texts at 2 parts each need 6, so the third text is refused after the sender was told it went. The message also says 'this account can send 5 more today', which means 5 parts, not 5 texts. Suggested fix: compute the parts of each text that will go (textParts(linkTextIn(...)) per recipient) and compare their sum with left. Word it as 'This would use 6 text message parts and this account has 5 left today (a text is 1 to 4 parts).'

new_bugs.title: The refusal says 'used all 200 text messages' when it means 200 parts
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts line 217; also /help line 268 and README SMS_DAILY_PER_ACCOUNT
new_bugs.detail: After about 100 two-part texts, the sender reads 'This account has used all 200 text messages this server sends for one account in a day.' They know they sent about 100, so the sentence is untrue to them. The parts explanation only comes after it. Suggested words: 'This account has used today's 200 text message parts. Most texts are 2 parts; one with letters outside the basic Latin set uses more. Nothing was sent.' Then {room} and {without}.

done.item: 1. Skeptic 19 and new bug (low): the time-stamp rest did not protect signers who finish at the same moment, and the copy said 'one signer in ten minutes'
done.how: src/server/tsa.ts now records every request to a service that is still waiting for an answer. A request sent while another is still out ends when the first one's 3 seconds are up, so signers who finish together wait together and never longer than the first. A request that would get under 250 ms is not sent, and the record says why. A healthy service is still asked by everyone. The rest stays in process memory, and the tsa.ts comment, README (Waiting) and .env.example now say plainly that a restart or a second process waits once more.
done.test: tests/open-signing.test.ts 'signers who finish at the same moment while a time-stamp service hangs wait together': two signers at once plus one a second later all finish before 3.6 s, with the right reason for each. The next signer gets no fetch and no wait. Three concurrent calls to a service that answers all reach it. The README and tsa.ts no longer say 'one signer in ten minutes'.
done.left_open: The rest is still per process. Several server processes, or a restart, each make one signer wait up to 4 s. Sharing it would mean putting it in the database, which I did not do because the harm is low.

done.item: 1. WhatsApp sending (src/server/whatsapp.ts)
done.how: New whatsapp.ts. Two providers: the Meta WhatsApp Business Platform (approved templates with three blanks: sender, document, link; WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_INVITE/_REMIND/_DONE, plus an optional _DEADLINE and _LANGUAGE) and a Twilio WhatsApp sender (TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM; an HX content template id or the plain text). There is also a dev outbox (WHATSAPP_DEV_OUTBOX). Every message is recorded in wa_messages. The number stays on the row only until the provider takes it. A message the provider would not take is tried again by the timer (cron.ts retryWhatsApp) and decided again at that moment. A refusal for good is put in the audit trail and the sender is emailed. There are four texts (invite, reminder, closes soon, completed). Each names the sender and says 'Reply STOP'. The completed one is a link and never the PDF. The texts are in src/lib/channels.ts WA_TEXTS and printed in README for the operator to get approved.

done.item: 3. STOP via POST /whatsapp/webhook, signature checked
done.how: routes-whatsapp.ts. Meta: JSON signed with X-Hub-Signature-256 using WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET; without the secret the request is refused. Twilio: a form signed with X-Twilio-Signature using TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN over APP_URL/api/whatsapp/webhook. GET answers the hub.challenge only when WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN is set (a new setting, needed by Meta). STOP and its variants stop WhatsApp to that number from every account that wrote to it (wa_stops, like text_stops), drop messages still waiting for another try, and are written to the audit trail. START lifts the stop. Email is not affected.

build:ds-channels.notes_for_integrator: Neither WhatsApp nor calls has been tried against a live provider; tests use fetch stubs only. Before relying on it, an operator needs a verified Meta business with approved templates (texts in README 'WhatsApp and codes by phone call') or a Twilio WhatsApp sender, plus Twilio Voice for calls. The webhook must point at APP_URL/api/whatsapp/webhook. New tables: wa_messages, wa_usage, wa_stops, voice_calls (all in SCHEMA). New recipient columns are appended to COLUMNS: wa_link, wa_agreed_at, wa_agreed_for, wa_sent_at, wa_sent_to. The design choice to review: voice is a 'Call me with the code' button on the sms_code screen (following the designer's note), not a separate 'call_code' check. Other limits: WhatsApp goes with email, not instead of it; it is not offered on templates, bulk sends or forms; switching it on during a correction of an envelope that is out sends with the next reminder. Each is named in README 'What is not in it'. Abuse cases covered by tests: forged STOP or status webhooks (403), spam to numbers with a false tick (daily limit, 4 per number per day, STOP, pause), call bombing (same limits as code texts plus 6 calls an hour per link). Not covered: an unpaid account messaging many different numbers within WHATSAPP_DAILY_PER_ACCOUNT. Two failures are not mine and still need their owners: src/server/pdfa.ts is missing from the whitepaper crypto inventory, and the README VPAT line fails gov-g01.

done.item: 4. Text for scanned pages: OCR_CMD (Tesseract) or OCRMYPDF_URL, background job with timeout, document language when known, serving search, text view and screen readers, never replacing the page, with the warning
done.how: New src/server/ocr.ts and src/server/routes-ocr.ts (GET /sign/:token/ocr, guarded exactly like /doc). Readings are stored in a new ocr_jobs table in SCHEMA; a trigger deletes a file's job row and its text whenever the file is deleted. Upload (routes-envelopes.ts) and page edits (pages.ts) queue the pages that have no text, a job runs straight after, and cron.ts picks up anything left over. With OCR_CMD, each page's own embedded image is passed to the command (JPEG as is, Flate images rebuilt as PNG) without a shell, and stopped after OCR_TIMEOUT_MS. With OCRMYPDF_URL, the PDF is POSTed with ?lang= and the text is read from the PDF that comes back. The service is on the outside-connections list. The language comes from a recipient's locale on an envelope using the file, else the account default, else English. A failed job is retried 3 times. Text is cleaned of control characters, capped per page, stored encrypted when FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set, and appended to files.text so search finds it. TextView shows OCR_WARNING first, then the text, and says when reading is still in progress. scanWarning in src/lib/scans.ts now has 'reading' and 'read' variants, and the API adds an 'ocr' state on File and Document. The signed PDF is never changed.
done.test: ds-a11y.test.ts: zero setup gives no job and no 'ocr' key. A stub command reads a PNG of the right size in deu, search finds the word, the sign route returns the text with the warning, and the file hash is unchanged. A JPEG goes through as .jpg, a typed PDF is not queued, a blank page gives empty text. A hanging reader is stopped at the timeout and marked failed after 3 tries. The command runs without a shell and output is cleaned. Access: 404 for an unknown token, 401 behind an access code, 403 once the envelope is declined. Service variant tested with a stubbed fetch, including retry on a non-PDF answer. Deleting the file deletes the job. A browser check with a stub reader showed the warning and text in the text view at 390 and 1280 px with no axe issues.
done.left_open: No limit per account on OCR work: one account uploading many 500-page scans can keep the single serial queue busy for others. Scans stored as CCITT fax images are skipped with OCR_CMD (OCRMYPDF_URL handles them). An image of up to 60M pixels is inflated in memory. OCR text is not written into the signed PDF and is not shown to the sender, only used for search. The language is usually the account's, because files are read before anyone is added to the envelope.

I read whatsapp.ts. hand() sends a Meta template with 3 parameters or a Twilio ContentSid/Body. deliver() clears to_phone once a message is sent. retryWhatsApp decides each message again through stillMay(). gaveUp() writes the audit line and emails the sender. As I recall Meta's rules, Meta does not approve a template that starts or ends with a variable, so the operator's submissions would probably be rejected. I could not check this against Meta.

checks.item: 2. Link by WhatsApp only with the sender's tick (bound to the number, in the audit trail); not for groups, forms or copies; never together with the text link
checks.evidence: Test 2/2b passes: the tick is bound to a fingerprint of the number and refused for templates, groups, copies, in-person signers and text_link at create. My probe H: POST /envelopes/:id/correct {text_link:true} on a person who already has WhatsApp answers 200 and leaves text_link=1 and wa_link=1. In probe H2 a reminder then sent both a text and a WhatsApp message. Probe I: POST /correct {whatsapp:true, whatsapp_agreed:true} answers 200 {ok:true}, but wa_link stays 0 and nothing is sent: the request is silently ignored. 'Instead of email' is not built, and the builder admits it.
checks.still_broken: The correction endpoint skips assertWhatsApp and waProblem, so text_link and WhatsApp can both be on. The same endpoint silently drops the whatsapp fields. The 'instead of email' choice is not built.
checks.suggested_fix: In correctWithCheck (or the /correct route), refuse text_link:true while wa_link is on, and the other way round. Either make /correct accept whatsapp and whatsapp_agreed through saveWhatsApp(correcting=true), or refuse them with a 400 that names PUT /envelopes/:id. Add both cases to the tests.

checks.item: 3. STOP via signed POST /whatsapp/webhook stops WhatsApp from that account, kept like text_stops
checks.evidence: The signature checks hold: a forged Meta post gets 403, a Twilio form without TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN gets 403 (probe G), and GET without WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN gets 403. Probe A: accounts A and B each sent WhatsApp to +44 7700 900801. One STOP wrote 2 wa_stops rows, and B's envelope shows 'WhatsApp stopped' and 'Not sent: they replied STOP'. Test 4 is named 'not other accounts' but uses a different number, so it does not test this. The brief asks for 'from that account'. The message says 'no more messages about documents from {sender}'. /security and README line 348 say 'from that account'. README line 1983 and openapi say 'every account'.
checks.still_broken: One STOP stops every account that ever wrote to that number. A signer who stops a stranger also loses WhatsApp from their real landlord or employer, and that sender is told 'they replied STOP' to them, which is untrue. The copy is inconsistent.
checks.suggested_fix: Stop only the account of the message being answered: Meta's messages[].context.id and Twilio's OriginalRepliedMessageSid identify it. Fall back to the latest account that wrote to the number when neither is present. Then make the test use the same number for both accounts. If stopping every account is kept on purpose, say so in WA_TEXTS, /security and README line 348.

checks.item: 4. Status words: Sent, Delivered to the phone, read never shown

checks.item: 5. Daily limit per account, automatic pause, masked certificate line
checks.evidence: The limit holds: 429 at send (test 5), and 4 per number per day holds (probe F: 6 envelopes, 4 messages sent). The pause holds messages back. The certificate line is masked. The sender's page reads 'Link also goes by WhatsApp to' followed by an empty number (Recipients.tsx line 307 with phone null).
checks.suggested_fix: In passCheckOn (signercode.ts) or reassignRecipient, set wa_link=0, wa_agreed_at/for=NULL and wa_sent_to=NULL, and write a 'WhatsApp switched off' audit line. Do the same in correctWithCheck when the person or the phone changes. Add a probe like B to the tests.

checks.item: 4. OCR of scanned pages: background job with timeout, document language, search, text view with the warning, page never replaced
checks.evidence: The happy path holds in a real browser. I set OCR_CMD to a stub node script and uploaded a PNG; the upload answered ocr:'queued' and the job finished as 'done'. Search with ?q=STUBWORD found the envelope. The text view at 390 and 1280 px showed the warning first, then the text. A planted U+202E (right-to-left override) character was removed, and <script> showed as plain text. GET /sign/:token/ocr uses the same find() and assertViewable() as /doc. ds-a11y.test.ts passes 13 tests. But there is a crash risk in imageOf() in src/server/ocr.ts. For a FlateDecode image with no predictor, it calls zlib.inflateSync(bytes) with no maxOutputLength and checks the size only afterwards. My probe (tests/out/verify-ds-a11y/bomb.ts) built a 2.1 MB PDF whose 100x100 image inflates to 2 GB. imageOf took 4.5 s and the process reached 4.4 GB of memory. The upload limit is 25 MB, so any free account can make the server run out of memory by uploading one such page while OCR_CMD is set.
checks.still_broken: The decompression bomb in imageOf (see the first new bug). Also, tick() awaits runOcr() whenever an OCR batch is running, so the cron run and POST /cron can wait for hours (see the second new bug).
checks.suggested_fix: Change the call to zlib.inflateSync(bytes, { maxOutputLength: row * h + 1 }) inside a try, and skip the page if it fails. In cron.ts, start runOcr() without awaiting it, for example `ocr_read: (void runOcr().catch(...), 'started')`, or await it with a short time limit.

new_bugs.title: Decompression bomb in OCR image extraction can run the server out of memory
new_bugs.where: src/server/ocr.ts imageOf(): `const raw = zlib.inflateSync(bytes);` (Flate image, predictor 1)
new_bugs.detail: The output size is not limited. The `raw.length < row*h` check runs only after the stream is fully inflated. Probe tests/out/verify-ds-a11y/bomb.ts: a 2.1 MB PDF with a 100x100 DeviceGray image whose stream inflates to 2 GB took the process to 4.4 GB of memory in 4.5 s. Uploads may be 25 MB, so one page can ask for far more memory than that. The job starts by itself right after any account's upload (queueOcr, then setTimeout, then runOcr) whenever OCR_CMD is set. No test covers it.

new_bugs.detail: The new selector has more class selectors than the phone rule, so it wins on phones too. keyboard-sign.cjs at 390 px logs the optional tick box at hw:24, hh:24. new_bugs.title: The cron run waits for the whole OCR queue to finish
new_bugs.where: src/server/cron.ts tickOnce(): `ocr_read: await runOcr()`; runOcr returns the shared promise when a batch is already running
new_bugs.detail: One batch can hold 5 files of up to 500 pages each, at up to 60 s per page, so it can run for hours. If one runs (started by an upload or an earlier tick), each 15-minute tick and each external POST /cron (the CRON_SECRET scheduler) hangs until it ends. External schedulers time out and report failure. noteTick(ok) is not called for that run, and ticks pile up. The other jobs still run, because ocr_read comes last.

new_bugs.title: A missing Tesseract or language pack fails silently, while the statement says pages are read
new_bugs.where: src/server/ocr.ts runOcr / readWithCommand; src/app/accessibility/page.tsx OCR line
new_bugs.detail: If `tesseract` is not installed, or the account's language pack (for example deu) is missing, every job fails 3 times. The error is stored only in ocr_jobs.error: nothing is logged, there is no startup check and no health line, and there is no fallback to eng. Meanwhile /accessibility tells signers that 'Pages that are pictures ... are read by a machine on this server'. Also, OCR_CMD is split on spaces, so a program path that contains a space cannot be used.

new_bugs.title: No OCR work limit per account; one file blocks the queue for everyone
new_bugs.detail: The builder already listed this. One serial queue reads up to 500 pages × OCR_TIMEOUT_MS per file, and a failed file is retried as a whole 3 times. That is up to about 25 hours for one 500-page file before other accounts' scans are read.

repair:ds-channels.notes_for_integrator:
Ways to abuse this, and how each is handled:
- A stranger replies STOP to cut someone off from their landlord: STOP now reaches only the quoted or latest account (4, 4c).
- A signer passes the document on to plant a false WhatsApp line on the certificate: WhatsApp ends on reassign (9).
- An API user turns on text and WhatsApp together through /correct: refused (9c).

Ways an honest person gets stuck, and how each is handled:
- A landline signer: the call is offered under 'Cannot get a code this way?' before any text is sent.
- After a reload on the call screen: the screen still says it was a call (9e).
- A sender ticks the text link for a WhatsApp person in Change person: the dialog switches WhatsApp off and says so.

Left open:
- There is no separate 'Code by phone call' check.
- No WhatsApp cap by plan, because that needs credits.ts, which this task does not own.
- The new template texts have not been checked against Meta.
- The Change person dialog's new line was checked by tsc only, not seen in a browser.
- The flows tool flags the new Connections card as P3 whenever the operator settings are on. It is correct with zero setup.

Shared files with small edits: signercode.ts (the import, a passCheckOn call, check.by in lockedView), routes-envelopes.ts (the /correct wrapper and the language shortcut), CheckPick.tsx (PhoneBox exported, callsOn prop), PersonMore.tsx, dialogs.tsx, Recipients.tsx, settings/page.tsx (one import, one line), AppShell.tsx (Me type).

checks.item: 1. Leaked-password check at sign-up, reset and change (range API, 5 SHA-1 chars, 3 s timeout, PWNED_CHECK, HIBP_RANGE_URL)
checks.evidence: I read pwned.ts and signinrules.ts. Only the prefix goes into the URL, with the Add-Padding header and redirect:'error'. Lines with a count of 0 are ignored. An answer that holds no list lines, or that times out, means 'not_checked', and the password is allowed. All three places that set a password call newPasswordOk: /auth/signup, /auth/reset and /me/password (I grepped every password_hash write). My probe (tests/out/verify-ds-sec-policy/probe.test.ts) showed three things: a lower-case list answer still refuses, with no users row made and only 5-character prefixes sent; a 302 from the list is not followed and the password is allowed; leaked-password refusal on change works. Browser: /signup at 390 px shows 'This password has appeared in a data leak. Choose another one.' The builder's 19/19 tests pass. /security shows the point only while pwnedUrl(process.env) is set, and outside.ts sets PWNED_CHECK=0 under OUTSIDE_CALLS=none.

After a longer password through /me/password, /envelopes opens. The owner with pw_below=64 still gets 200. Browser: the gate screen at 390 and 320 has no sideways scroll and no target under 44 px. The owner's card says 'Your own password is shorter than 24 characters...'.

This is low severity, since the brief only asks for the check at the next sign-in.

done.item: 1. src/server/pages.ts: apply remove / turn / move to one document
done.how: The rules live in src/lib/pages.ts, shared by server and editor. planPages: each op names a page as it is at that moment, counted from 1. Turns are 90, 180 or 270, and consecutive turns of one page merge into a single turn. Every refusal is a plain sentence: page out of range, removing the last page, an unknown op, more than 500 ops. moveFields: fields follow their page. On a turned page a field's middle turns with the content, and the field keeps its size in points and stays upright. Fields on removed pages come back as `dropped`. The server's remakeFile uses pdf-lib copyPages and setRotation, adding the new turn to any rotation the file already had. It stores a NEW file (the old one is never touched), reads its text again for search with scan pages and encryption as on upload, and records files.page_ops = {from, ops}, a new column added at the end of COLUMNS. Removing a page that has fields is refused with 409 code page_fields and the list of fields, unless drop_fields is true.

done.item: 2. POST /envelopes/:id/documents/:doc/pages for drafts and templates; for an envelope that is out, only through Correct with the sign-again choice
done.how: New file src/server/routes-pages.ts, imported in tests/helpers.ts boot() and src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts. Drafts go through saveDraft and envelopes that are out go through correctEnvelope, with resign passed on, so the existing 409 sign_again rule applies unchanged. Completed, declined, cancelled and expired envelopes are refused with 409 and "Copy it to send a new version." Also refused: another account's envelope or an unknown doc (404), a wording-locked template copy (403 via assertWordingKept), a held draft, and a document whose file changed while the new file was being made (409). Every request counts toward a limit of 120 an hour per account, because each one stores a file. With save:false only the file is made, which is what the editor uses. In that mode file_id may name an unsaved file the editor holds, as long as it is not a template file held back from this person (fileHeldBack); a file from another account is 404.

build:ds-page-tools.notes_for_integrator: How the editor saves pages: the editor never lets the server write to the envelope directly. It calls the route with save:false, swaps the file into its own state, and saves through the normal PUT. That is why drafts autosave as usual and corrections ask the existing sign-again question. The audit line comes from the files.page_ops chain, read by notePageChanges inside writeContent. Ways of misusing it, and what stops each: another account's envelope or file (404); reading a held-back template's file by passing it as file_id (fileHeldBack); filling storage with files (120 requests an hour per account, and refused requests store nothing); editing a signed document (409, or sign_again); an extreme number of ops (500 cap). Ways an honest person gets stuck, and what happens: removing a page with fields (asked first, with the list); turning a page all the way back round (the dialog just closes); someone already finished (note in the dialog plus the existing question); a file just replaced and not saved yet (accepted, with a correction line instead of a page line).

build:ds-seal-ltv.notes_for_integrator:
Ordering at Finish, with TSA_URL set: (1) the record's chain head is time-stamped, (2) the certificate is drawn and the seal applied, (3) after a B-T seal, the long-term step runs. Steps 1 and 2 share one 4-second budget for time stamps. Step 3 can add up to LTV_WAIT_MS (20 s by default) to the last signer's Finish when a responder hangs; the brief asks for that, and most responders answer in well under a second. Without TSA_URL nothing new runs.

Because of step 1, seal.test.ts now expects 2 calls to the time-stamp service where it used to expect 1. If someone changes when the record is stamped, those counts change too.

Nothing in billing was touched.

Things that need the operator: a production time-stamp service, plus a seal certificate whose chain names OCSP or revocation-list addresses. With a self-made certificate nothing long-term is added. Before relying on it, open a B-LTA file in Acrobat or the EU DSS validator. That has not been done.

Left open:
