new_bugs.title: The 'Next to:' hint repeats the printed blanks inside Easy reading
new_bugs.detail: In Easy reading the field box already sits right after its line, yet the signature box reads 'Signature (required) Next to: Signature: ____ Date: ____'. The raw underscores are noise for sighted readers and are read aloud to screen readers. Evidence: tests/out/ux-ds-reading-view/390-04-easy-full.png (bottom). new_bugs.title: A link on every part: 'See this on the page' gets heavy in long documents, and its screen-reader name only gives the page
new_bugs.detail: Every section, including the title, gets the link. A 2-page lease already has 4 (look.out), and a 20-page lease would have dozens of identical links. The aria-label 'See this on the page, page 2' does not say which part, so a screen reader's link list is a run of near-copies (charter P12: a repeated control names its item). Fix: name the section in the label ('See 1. Rent on page 1'). Skip the link on a part that has no heading, or on the title part.

new_bugs.title: Easy reading shows invisible text that is not on the pages that are signed

(b) POST /envelopes with template_id plus anchor fields or auto_tags answers 200 with no 'anchors' key and places nothing, with no word about it. checks.item: 2. Signing inside a site (registered origins, frame-ancestors, postMessage, audit line)
checks.evidence: Cross-site check: the app on localhost:4152 inside a portal on 127.0.0.1:4153. The CSP was 'frame-ancestors http://127.0.0.1:4153'. A full sign on a 390 px phone inside the frame worked. The portal received [origin http://localhost:4152, {source:'growsigning', event:'signing_complete'}]. The audit reads 'Signed', 'Signed inside a frame on http://127.0.0.1:4153', 'Envelope completed'. Account B gets 403 origin_not_listed when it uses account A's origin. A send-scope key gets 403 on POST /account/embed-origins. Origins are normalised (case, :443, trailing slash, IDN to punycode).
checks.still_broken: A signer who has an access code cannot sign inside a frame on another site. In the frame, POST /sign/:token/unlock with the right code answers 200, but the next GET /sign/:token still says locked:true. The ts_ac_ cookie is SameSite=Lax, so the browser does not send it from a cross-site iframe. On screen the person types the right code, presses Open document, and lands back on 'Enter your access code' with no explanation (code-2-after-phone.png). The email/SMS signer code (passCookie in signercode.ts) uses the same cookie() helper, so it very likely fails the same way (not run in the browser). /developers tells integrators to 'Use an access code or a code by email when that matters' in exactly this setup.
checks.suggested_fix: Until the unlock works without a third-party cookie, refuse frame_origin in recipient-view for a recipient with an access code or a signer code (400: 'This person has an access code, which cannot be typed inside a frame on another website. Send them the link by email, or remove the code.'), and correct the /developers line. A real fix would be a SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned cookie for embed links, or unlock state kept on the server per view.

checks.item: 3. Sender view (POST /envelopes/:id/sender-view)
checks.evidence: In the browser, cross-site, 390 px and 1280 px: the editor opens inside the portal without AppShell menus and with no sideways scroll (screen-phone.png, screen-desktop.png). The Next/Send steps sent the draft. The portal received {source:'growsigning', event:'sent', envelope_id}, the frame went to http://127.0.0.1:4153/done?event=sent, and the draft status became 'sent'. Server probes: a mismatched frame_origin/return_url gives a 400, another account gets 404, and the screen gets 403 on everything outside its draft.
checks.still_broken: (a) The session does not end on the server when the draft is sent. After POST /envelopes/:id/send through the screen, GET /me, /contacts and /envelopes/:id still answer 200, sender_views.ended_at stays null, and frame-ancestors still allows the origin until /embed/sender/close is called or an hour passes. Only the page's own close call ends it. (b) Through GET /files/:id/content the screen can read any file uploaded anywhere in the account after the screen opened, if it knows the id. (c) Editor load errors still router.replace('/app/envelopes') inside the frame (Editor.tsx lines 87, 97, 114). (d) The 60-per-hour limit per IP on /embed/sender/open can block an office behind one NAT.
checks.suggested_fix: Call endSenderView inside the send route when auth.via==='embed'. Limit the file check to files uploaded by this session (store session_hash on the file or record ids at upload). In embedded mode, call embedded.onDone('closed') instead of router.replace on load errors.

checks.item: 3. Round-trip importer: re-verifies chains, marks records 'imported from <deployment>; chain verified|not verified', refuses out-for-signature
checks.evidence: The mechanics work: suite tests 5-8 and 13 pass, and my P1 import gave 200 with ids mapped. But tests/out/verify-g19/probe.test.ts P1 shows the marks can be forged. (a) deployment.url is self-asserted. I set it to https://growsigning.com and the record banner reads 'Imported from growsigning.com on 21 Nov 2026; chain verified.' (b) The chain formula (HASH_HOW) has no secret, so I rewrote the signer to 'Jane Doe, Mayor', put in a forged PDF, recomputed the hashes, and got chain_ok=true. (c) data.imported[] is carried over almost verbatim. A forged entry with source 'docusign', chain_ok true and the banner 'Signed on GrowSigning and verified by GrowSigning. This signature is legally valid.' was stored and shown with that text. (d) chainHolds skips the hash check on every line whose redacted_at equals the envelope's purged_at, so any history passes (P4 returned ok:true).
checks.still_broken: The importer turns attacker-supplied claims into this server's own marks. The rule 'an import never invents evidence' is broken.
checks.suggested_fix: Say 'the export says it came from <host>' rather than 'Imported from <host>'. Explain 'chain verified' as internal consistency only, or sign exports with a server key and verify that key. Rebuild the banner for data.imported records from a fixed template (source + date); never use r.banner, and drop chain_ok for docusign records. Only skip a redacted line's hash check when detail is actually empty or redacted.

checks.item: 4. DocuSign importer: archived records only, exact banner, never on /verify as completed here, templates mapped, rest listed
checks.evidence: Fixture tests pass, and the real-looking Lease fixture got the exact brief banner (screenshot 6). Probe P2 and screenshot 12-record-random.png: a plain PDF with no envelope ID and no certificate ('Holiday photo scan.pdf') is stored as status 'completed'. Its banner says 'Imported from DocuSign ... Signed there, not here', and the record shows 'Status where it was signed: completed'. Public /verify of that file then says 'An account here brought this exact file in from DocuSign ... It was signed there, not here'. That is invented evidence: nothing shows it came from DocuSign or was signed at all. Not checked against real DocuSign downloads (the builder says so).
checks.still_broken: Any PDF can be laundered into a 'signed on DocuSign, completed' record and a public /verify answer.
checks.suggested_fix: Do not accept a PDF that has neither a DocuSign envelope ID nor a Certificate Of Completion; list it as not brought in. Or mark it 'file brought in, no sign it was signed', with status null. Leave such files out of /verify, or say only 'an account uploaded this file'.

new_bugs.title: Forged export makes this server vouch, on public /verify, for a forged PDF from any named server
new_bugs.where: src/server/importer.ts importExport / chainHolds / storeRecord; src/lib/exportfull.ts verifyImportedWords; routes-account.ts /public/verify
new_bugs.detail: Steps (probe P1): take a real export, set deployment.url to https://growsigning.com, swap the signed PDF for a forged one, rewrite the actor names, recompute the hashes with the public HASH_HOW formula, rebuild the manifest, then import into any account (sign-up is free and the signer-up is the owner). Public /verify of the forged PDF returns imported {source:'growsigning', from:'growsigning.com', chain_ok:true}, and the page says 'its history was checked and still led from line to line, and the export named this file as its signed PDF.' The manifest and the chain prove only internal consistency, never origin.

done.item: HIGH: anchored fields stall the server (event loop)
done.how: src/lib/anchors.ts: new ANCHOR_FIELDS_MAX=200. findText now reads each page's lines once (a WeakMap cache), builds the RegExp once per call instead of once per line, and skips lines that do not contain the first word. src/server/anchors.ts: more than 200 anchored fields are refused (400 too_many_anchors) before any PDF is read. The field loop gives other requests a turn every 20 anchors. A scan that times out now destroys the pdf.js loading task, so it stops working in the background.
done.test: tests/ds-dev-api.test.ts 'anchors: more than the most are refused...': 201 anchors are refused in under 1.5 s and nothing is saved. 200 anchors over a 40-page, 45-line PDF finish under 8 s (well under that in practice). 'findText reads each page once...' checks the cache gives the same answers and that regex characters are matched literally.
done.left_open: 200 anchors is a fixed number, not a time budget, so very large PDFs (500 pages) still take real CPU per request. The PDF reading itself (scanPdf) still runs on the main thread.

done.how: An admin gives the counter permission person by person and marks templates for the counter in Settings > Team > More options > Service counter. The template must have someone who signs in person. With that done, Counter appears under More, and only for people who have the permission. The page has three parts. 'Someone new' (pick the template, type the person's name and an email for their copy, press Start) makes the document from the template and sends it. 'Waiting' lists everyone still due to sign in person on counter documents, with buttons Start, Continue, or Confirm when a second official is needed; Start on another official's person takes them over and the audit trail says so. 'Finished today' lists the last 24 hours with a Receipt button. 'Connect the citizen's screen' shows a 6-character code and its QR code (made with the existing qr module), good for one use within 10 minutes. The person's screen at /counter/screen waits until the identity check is recorded, then opens the signing page. The official sees progress as counts only; what the person types is shown only if an admin allows it for that template.

done.item: 2. Identity check by the official
done.how: The one question is 'Which ID did you see?', answered with 'An identity document' (its kind or Other, exactly the last 4 letters or digits, and who issued it) or 'Nothing: I know this person'. The official ticks "I checked this person's identity as recorded above." That goes into the audit trail in their name and onto the certificate as their statement, with the line 'GrowSigning cannot check an identity document...'. Until the check is recorded, every /sign/:token call for that person answers 423 counter_id_first on any device (a counterGate call in look() in routes-sign.ts). A mistake can be corrected before Finish, and the trail keeps both records. A picture of the ID document is offered only when the account switches it on, and that switch only exists when FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set. The picture is stored encrypted in the visit's own database row (sealFile), listed in the evidence pack as counter/id-document-*, and removed by the timer once the document is purged.

done.item: 3. Help with signing (accommodations) and the witness rule
done.how:
Four kinds, each the official's statement in the audit trail and on the certificate (counterCertLines, one line added in pdf.ts):
- Signs with a mark: needs the existing witness role for this person on the document. The official may be that witness only if the account switches it on (off by default). This is checked when the mark is recorded and again at Finish.
- Someone signs for them: Finish answers 409 until a second official with the counter permission confirms with their own login (the same official is refused).
- Read aloud: needs the language.
- Interpreter: needs the name and language.
A mark and someone signing for the person cannot both be recorded. 'Take back' works before Finish: the item leaves the certificate and stays in the trail. The evidence pack gets counter.txt with every statement.

build:g18.notes_for_integrator:
Abuse checks, each with a test:
- guessing the pairing code: per-address limit, one use, 10 minutes, unused code replaced
- reaching the counter from another account, as a member without the permission, or with an API key: 404 or 403
- the official making themselves the witness, or changing that rule after recording: checked again at Finish
- one official confirming their own 'signs for them': refused
- a finished person's screen getting the link back: never given again

Ways an honest person gets stuck, also tested:
- wrong ID recorded: re-record before Finish
- code expired: make a new one
- colleague on a break: take over, which is audited
- no second official: Finish says so in words; 'Take back' is available

Left open:

For an in-person signer who had a counter visit, it gives the recipient a new signing token and writes the audit line 'Counter link closed'. The link used on the tablet or the official's device then answers 404 (UnknownLink card) for the page, the document and the download. The completed email is built after this, so it carries the new link that only the person has. Ordinary in-person signing outside the counter is unchanged. On the sign page, for counter signers (env.counter present), the done card shows CounterCopy ('Your copy, with its certificate, is on its way to the email address you gave.') with no View or Download buttons. On the citizen's own screen the tree celebration is gone and 'Hand the screen back / Next person' sits right under it (Next person at y=586 on a 390x844 phone, screenshot 17-p-sign-done.png).

done.how: counterGate now refuses with 423 counter_id_first whenever there is no open visit with id_at and the person is a counter signer. A counter signer is an in-person recipient with any counter_visits row, or on an envelope whose template is in counter_templates for that account (isCounterEnvelope). So a document sent the ordinary way from a counter template, or opened from the official's 'Host an in-person signing' email before Start, opens on no device.

repair:g18.notes_for_integrator: 1) The busy-file edits are small. envelopes.ts has one import and one line, counterFinished(e, r), just before 'await advance(e.id)' in completeRecipient. It must stay before advance(), because the completed email reads the token. This creates an envelopes.ts <-> counter.ts import cycle, the same pattern witness.ts already uses (function-level only). 2) The sign page has five small conditions on env.counter / env.counter?.screen, plus the counter_id_first route to CounterWait. counterFacts now returns { counter: { screen: boolean, envelope_id } } for every counter signer, not only on the counter screen, so the done card never offers the closed link's download. 3) The screenshots in tests/out/repair-g18/ come from walk.cjs and print.cjs, adapted from the reviewer's and skeptic's scripts. Look at 05b, 08, 15, 16, 17, 17a, 23 and 03. 4) The dev server is stopped. .next-repair-g18 and its DATA_DIR are deleted, and only my .next-repair-g18 lines were removed from tsconfig.json. Lines other engineers' dev servers added are left. 5) Abuse and stuck cases, handled by tests: the next person opens the old link from history (404); a counter document sent the normal way to skip the ID check (423); the tablet dies mid-visit (Connect another screen); a declined signer told they finished ('closed' state); an office behind one NAT (limit 100). Left open and named under the items: no global pairing limit across addresses; values readable through the sender API by design; no email means no counter service; the official's own device reload after Finish shows 'link not recognised'.

GET /envelopes/<Ben's envelope> returns 200 with shared {owner:'Ben Okoro',level:'manage'}. The share row keeps ended_at NULL, and isActive() checks only current membership. Months later a rehire silently regains manage/send rights nobody gave again. The README says 'A share stops by itself when either person leaves the account', and the builder's test comment says 'also if she were to come back', but the test only checks while she is away. The same applies when the owner leaves and comes back.

new_bugs.title: 'see' colleague is offered per-person and comment buttons that the server refuses

new_bugs.detail: Screenshot v03-see-person-more-phone.png shows Change person, QR code, Share on WhatsApp and Text to a 'see' colleague. QR code answers with the not_in_share refusal (v08). The page notice also tells them 'Share each link yourself: it is in each person's More'. EnvelopeComments is not filtered by shareAllows, so Send comment, Answer and Mark as settled appear and end in a 403 (they need 'manage'). This breaks 'no dead buttons'. new_bugs.title: An envelope deleted after signing can still be moved by its sender
new_bugs.detail: Probe P2: hidden_at is set, then POST /envelopes/:id/move by the owner answers 200 {moved:1} and changes sender_id. The rule elsewhere is 'gone for the sender: no list, no search, no change'. The new owner does not see it (404), so nothing leaks, but ownership of a removed record changes without an admin.

new_bugs.title: A draft handed over with Send for is lost to its maker when the share ends
new_bugs.detail: Probe P8: Ana makes a draft and picks 'Send for Ben', so the draft becomes Ben's. Ben then ends the share. Ana now gets 404 opening the draft, so the editor (where 'From me' lives) cannot be reached. Only a direct API call to POST /envelopes/:id/send-for with an empty on_behalf_of gets it back (200). An honest person loses sight of their draft with no hint. While the share is active, the draft also leaves Ana's own Documents list and shows only under 'Shared with me by Ben'.

new_bugs.title: Templates and several chosen envelopes cannot be moved from the screen
new_bugs.detail: The brief says 'moves chosen envelopes or templates'. The API (POST /envelopes/move) supports it, but the UI has only the single-envelope More line and the admin's move-everything. A member cannot hand over one template on screen.

checks.item: 1. BILLING_MODE=deployment: nothing counted/held/expiring, no Stripe call, plan routes 404, Settings Plan one agreement line, sending unlimited
checks.evidence: Holds: gov-g14 14/14 pass. On my dev server (port 4142, BILLING_MODE=deployment) GET /api/billing and POST /api/stripe/webhook answer 404 with the plain sentence. Settings > Plan on desktop shows only the Agreement card with the right line. STRIPE_* are deleted at start and on every request, and /me says billing.enabled=false. Fails: my probe tests/out/verify-g14/probe.test.ts sent 51 one-signer envelopes to new citizens from a fresh agency account on day one, and number 51 was refused with 429: 'In its first week, an account that has not paid can send to 50 people a day ... To lift the limit, use the contact form'. hasNotPaid() is true for every account on a deployment server, so the 50 a day (first week) and 200 a day limits, the fake-notice filters and paidTrustText ('stop applying once the account has a payment...') all still apply, and they talk about a payment that cannot happen there. The builder's 'sending has no limit' test sends only 6 envelopes, so it cannot catch this. The designer note for gov-G14 says 'never: signature counts, expiry or top-ups in deployment mode', but on the deployment server '/' shows 'US$1 a signature, or US$9 a month', /pricing shows Grove and top-ups, /help explains expiry and refunds of top-ups, and the public footer says 'What you pay, less card fees, goes to Treegens tree planting' and links 'Stop a subscription'. The guarded call in credits.ts was not written (it depends on env deletion instead).
checks.still_broken: Daily recipient limits and the unpaid-account wording on deployment servers. Raising UNPAID_DAILY_RECIPIENTS (the README's advice) does nothing in an account's first week, because NEW_ACCOUNT_DAILY_RECIPIENTS=50 rules then. Consumer price, top-up and expiry copy still appears on landing, /pricing, /help and the footer. The operator Review queue still shows the Billing card with dead buttons (see new_bugs).
checks.suggested_fix: hasNotPaid() (or dailyCap/limitWords) should treat isDeploymentBilling() as trusted, or at least lift the recipient cap and drop the pay-to-lift wording. This needs the envelopes.ts owner. Hide the consumer price, top-up and expiry blocks and the Billing operator card when isDeploymentBilling() is on, and add a test that sends to more than 50 new people on day one.

new_bugs.title: senderRich drops or swaps any digits in a variable, so account names with numbers render wrong in the sidebar
new_bugs.where: src/components/senderLang.tsx senderRich, used by AppShell.tsx:158 shell.impact with {account: me.account.name}
new_bugs.detail: senderRich replaces each React part with its bare index ('0', '1', ...), then splits the translated text on /(\d+)/ and treats every run of digits as a part index. The account name is passed as a plain variable, so its digits are read as indexes. I ran the same logic (tests/out/verify-ds-lang-sender/rich.ts). For account 'Studio 54' it gives '[12] sheets of paper saved by Studio [undefined]': the digits disappear. For 'Team 0' it gives '... saved by Team [12]': the sheet count appears in place of the 0. Before this change, AppShell printed {me.account.name} directly, so this is a regression in English with zero setup, for any account big enough to show the paper total. A translated string that contains a digit would break the same way. Fix: use markers that cannot occur in text (for example \u0001i\u0002), and add a test with a digit in a variable.

done.item: 2. Answers kept in the visitor's browser and, for a day, on the server for that browser only
done.how: New table form_drafts (db.ts SCHEMA). It is keyed by powerform and a random browser id held in an HMAC-sealed cookie ts_wf_<form>. It is kept for powerformIdleHours (a day), or for the shared-device minutes, and purged on every visit and by the timer (cron.ts form_answers_forgotten). Only answers to the form's own questions are kept, each at most 4000 characters, 64000 in all (413). One connection keeps at most 20 sets and the oldest goes, so nobody is refused. Saves are limited to 600 an hour per connection. The page also keeps answers in localStorage (try/catch) and restores them with one line and a 'Start again' button. A shared-device form never hands answers back: GET returns null, the page deletes them on open, and localStorage is not used.

build:ds-web-forms.notes_for_integrator: Design choice: the charter merges 'Anyone with this link can sign' and 'fill-in form' into one Form, so every public form whose open role has fill-in fields now asks them as questions (on every screen size, no layout choice) and shows the document before the envelope is made. Attacker cases handled: forged or other-browser cookie (test), oversize answers (413, test), draft flooding (20 per connection plus a rate limit, test), scam text in answers mailed to a typed victim address (fake-notice filter, test), bypassing page checks by calling /start directly (re-checked, test), setting the signature or another person's field through answers (ignored, test), next person on a shared tablet reading answers (test). Honest-person cases handled: reload or closed page (answers return, screenshot 11), a condition hiding an answered question (answer dropped, test), a form paused mid-way (plain 404 words, test). Left open: a botnet with many addresses can still fill form_drafts for up to a day (bounded per address only); answers in form_drafts are stored unencrypted for that day; review PDF rendering costs CPU per request (60 per 10 minutes per address); scrolling to the end is not proven to the server. The tiled 'NOT COMPLETED YET' stamp was left off the review copy because it made answers unreadable; instead the footer says it has no envelope and is not signed. Reviewers may want a lighter mark. new_bugs.title: A second start in the same browser discards the new answers and reopens the old envelope
new_bugs.where: src/server/routes-envelopes.ts POST /public/powerforms/:slug/start, the 'again' resume branch (before checkAnswers is used); src/server/webforms.ts dropDraft is not called on resume
new_bugs.detail: Probe P1 (tests/out/verify-ds-web-forms/probe.test.ts) and browser run v06 to v09: the person starts with Town='Old town', goes back to the form, types the same name and email, answers Town='New town', sees 'New town' in the review and presses Continue to sign. The response is {resumed:true}, and the signing page field holds 'Old town'. The draft row is left behind (count 1). This breaks 'what you reviewed is what you sign'. An honest person correcting a typo is the most likely way to hit it.

new_bugs.title: Review shows the server draft, not what will be submitted, when a save failed
new_bugs.where: src/app/f/[slug]/page.tsx keep() and onDone; src/server/routes-webforms.ts GET review uses readDraft
new_bugs.detail: keep() catches every error: it shows 413 and 429 but still moves on to the review, and it silently ignores network failures. The review PDF is then drawn from the older server copy, while sign() posts the current answers. So the document checked can differ from the envelope made. The non-awaited PUTs from onStep can also land after the final awaited PUT and overwrite it with fewer answers.

new_bugs.title: Shared-device answers can still be read through /review by the next person at the tablet
new_bugs.detail: Probe P5: on a shared-device form, GET /draft returns null, but GET /review with the same browser cookie returns the PDF with the previous person's answers (22988 bytes against 22411 empty) for up to 60 minutes if that person abandoned the form. The page DELETEs the draft when it opens, which covers the normal path. Someone who types the API URL, or opens it before the page loads, still gets the PDF.

new_bugs.title: Anyone with the link can render the template document without typing any details
new_bugs.detail: Probe P3: a fresh client with no cookie gets a 200 PDF of the full template (60 per 10 minutes per IP). Before this change the document was only visible after a start, with its limits. This is probably acceptable for a public form, but it is a new exposure and CPU cost that is not named in left_open.

new_bugs.title: Saves are rate-limited per connection across all forms at 600 an hour
new_bugs.detail: A front desk or school on one NAT, where about 60 people an hour each answer 10 questions, hits 429. The words are kind, but the person is then sent to a review drawn from stale answers (see the medium bug above). There is no larger bucket for shared-device forms, unlike starts.

done.item: 5. Date from another date
done.how: A date field with date_from {from, add, unit}, placed with 'Date from another date' under More fields. The panel offers Counted from, How many, Of (days/weeks/months) and Before or after, and says the rule in words. The calendar is Gregorian and month ends are clamped (31 Jan + 1 month = 28/29 Feb). A date-signed source counts from the calendar day of signing in the signer's device zone, falling back to the sender's zone, then UTC: the same day the date signed prints. The server works out the value on save and finish and ignores the browser's value. These fields are never required and never hold sender wording. A draft can keep a rule with no source yet; send refuses with what to do (kindsProblem). The note under the field reads 'Counted on the calendar. done.item: 3. 'Paid' only after Stripe's webhook confirms for that connected account; 'Payment started, not confirmed' before; pay-before completes the part only on confirmation; refunds and disputes shown
done.how: payFirst runs synchronously inside completeRecipient, so nothing is awaited between the look and the claim. It checks the Finish as Finish would, inside a rolled-back transaction, stores the body, and answers 402 with code pay_first. The webhook's signature is checked, it must be 5 minutes old or less, and each event id is applied once. The event must name the payment's own connected account, and Stripe is asked again that the session is paid for the same amount and currency. Only then is the payment marked paid, and finishAfterPayment completes the part with the stored body. If the document changed or closed in the meantime, nothing is signed: the signer is emailed and does not pay twice, and the sender is emailed about a refund when the document closed. When Stripe's page shows paid before the webhook arrives, the answer is { waiting: true }, never paid. A person can have only one open Stripe page at a time. Refunds (partial or full) and disputes (open, won, lost) from the webhook appear on the document page (src/components/sender/CollectNote.tsx) and in its history. After paying an amount taken from a field, a Finish with a different amount is refused.

settings: STRIPE_CONNECT_CLIENT_ID: the Stripe Connect client id (ca_...). The redirect address is https://<host>/api/collect/callback.
STRIPE_CONNECT_SECRET_KEY: the platform's secret key used for Connect calls. Unset, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is used.

STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET: the signing secret of the Connect webhook endpoint at /api/collect/webhook. Events: checkout.session.completed, async_payment_succeeded, async_payment_failed, expired, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created, updated, closed, account.application.deauthorized.
All three are needed, or nothing offers the feature. It is always off with BILLING_MODE=deployment.
build:ds-pay-collect.notes_for_integrator:
The charter puts Take payments in a Settings > Connections section. That section does not exist, and adding it would take an admin to 11 sections (the cap is 10), so I put the card in Sending, next to ChannelsStatus, the way the WhatsApp connections card already works. When Stripe is set up, Sending can then go over the 4-card rule. PayLinkChoice is now a wrapper around AskPayment, and the old card body is exported as PayLinkCard; the ReviewParts.tsx source-text tests stay green. In /security I renamed 'No payment collection.' to 'No money passes through us.', and in README the 'Payments are not collected' line became 'GrowSigning never holds money: ...'. I updated both regexes in tests/gaps-industry.test.ts. Nothing in routes-billing.ts or credits.ts was touched. 

Open risks: (a) the Stripe calls are only checked against a stand-in, never live; (b) signer words are not run through t(); (c) there is no GrowSigning receipt email and no account webhook for payments; (d) one payment is asked of each person who signs and is not on the sender's team, and there is no way to choose a single payer; (e) a person passed the document by reassignment is keyed by email, so a new address starts a new payment row; (f) collect_payments.session_id is UNIQUE, so if Stripe ever returned a duplicate id it would be a 500; (g) on the editor phone layout and Settings at 390px, nothing was looked at. Three attacker cases are covered by tests: forged, stale and replayed webhooks; a wrong connected account; and a changed amount after paying. Three honest-person cases are covered by tests: paying then closing the tab, Stripe being disconnected, and the document changing after payment. Two more were checked by screenshot only: Stripe unreachable, and coming back in a different tab.

done.item: 5. Cleaner scans: find the page edges (largest four-sided shape), straighten, raise contrast in the browser, with a way back; original photo stored with the document and listed in the evidence pack
done.how: Own code with no library: src/components/editor/scan.ts. It looks at the photo at about 480px, splits paper from background (Otsu threshold on brightness minus saturation), takes the largest blob with its holes filled, reduces its convex hull to 4 corners and refines each side with a line fit. It refuses (returns null) when the shape is not close to four-sided (fit 0.9 to 1.12, corners 50 to 130 degrees), fills over 92% or under 15% of the photo, or has weak contrast. It then straightens the page with a perspective transform and brightens it per block of the page (removes shadows, keeps ink colour muted). preparePhotos in photos.ts runs it per picture and sends scan_original_<n> and scan_cleaned along with the upload (one optional argument added to uploadFile in upload.ts). The server (src/server/scanphotos.ts, table scan_photos in db.ts SCHEMA, one call in storeUpload) keeps the photos, capped at 12 MB each and 40 MB in all. If any part is not a PNG or JPEG, it keeps nothing. Documents list cleaned_pages (one spread in loadEnvelope); signers never see it. The wording note says 'Undo cleanup', which takes priority over 'Use the photo as it was': CleanedLine.tsx under the file calls POST /files/:id/undo-cleanup, which rebuilds the document from the photos, and Ed.swapFile swaps it in. The evidence pack gets scan-photos/ with index.csv and a README line containing 'The page was cleaned from this photo'. Page edits carry the photos to the new file (one call in pages.ts). When a file is deleted a trigger notes its photos and sweepScanPhotos in cron removes them from disk.

done.item: 1. SAML 2.0 for an account: our metadata URL, ACS (HTTP-POST only), IdP metadata pasted or uploaded, with the library doing signature checks
done.how: Added @node-saml/node-saml (MIT, the library the brief names) and @xmldom/xmldom, which node-saml already installs, as a direct dependency for reading metadata. New files: src/server/saml.ts (our entity id per account at /api/sso/saml/sp/<random>, which also serves the metadata; reading IdP metadata; the SAML set-up; a SQLite cache provider; checkAnswer; beginSaml) and src/server/routes-saml.ts (GET metadata, POST /sso/saml/acs, GET /sso/saml/finish, PUT /account/sso/saml). Settings required: the assertion itself must be signed (wantAssertionsSigned), plus idpIssuer, audience = our entity id, validateInResponseTo always (the request ids live in saml_requests and are used once), rejectReplayedAssertions (saml_seen), and 30 s of clock skew. The library only warns about a wrong Recipient, so we check these again ourselves and refuse on failure: a bearer SubjectConfirmation with Recipient equal to our ACS, InResponseTo equal to this browser's request, NotOnOrAfter still ahead, and our Audience. The ACS checks the answer, keeps who it vouched for on the signin_states line for 2 minutes, then sends the browser on with a 303 to /finish. /finish needs the cookie set when the sign-in started (a Lax cookie is not sent on the provider's cross-site POST). It then calls finishOrgSignIn, which I pulled out of the OIDC callback in routes-orgsso.ts without changing it, so claimed domains, enforcement, the owner's way back in, join_new and 'Try a sign-in' are shared. org_idps gained a kind column ('oidc' or 'saml'); /sso/start and /account/sso/try hand SAML accounts to beginSaml. Moving from SAML back to OIDC asks for a client secret. Removing the service clears the metadata. UI: one Single sign-on card with a 'Standard' choice (OpenID Connect / SAML 2.0) in OrgSso.tsx, and the SAML part in the new OrgSaml.tsx: our two addresses, name, metadata pasted or read from a file in the browser, sign-in host and the date the certificate ends.

new_bugs.detail: scan_original_n is any PNG or JPEG the sender's client posts. My probe stored an unrelated JPEG as the 'original', with no link to the cleaned page checked. The pack then says 'The page was cleaned from this photo'. It should say the sender's browser supplied this photo as the one it cleaned the page from.

new_bugs.title: Undo cleanup can be repeated without limit on the same file
new_bugs.detail: The original file keeps its scan_photos, so each call on its id makes another new file (my probe got 200 three times with three new file ids). Each call rebuilds a PDF of up to 40 MB of photos. That is unbounded storage and CPU for a signed-in user. Answer with the existing undone file, or mark the original as undone.

new_bugs.title: Help promises the home-screen app keeps you signed in, which is false on iPhone
new_bugs.detail: An iOS home-screen web app has its own cookie storage, separate from Safari, so the person has to sign in again inside it. 'You stay signed in as you are in the browser' only holds on Android.

new_bugs.title: 'Origin: null' is dropped before the API's cross-site check
new_bugs.detail: A sandboxed or data: cross-site form sends 'Origin: null'. On browsers with no Sec-Fetch-Site (older Safari), deleting that header bypasses both the router Origin check and the Sec-Fetch-Site check. Only SameSite=Lax prevents CSRF. Better: drop it only when Sec-Fetch-Site is 'none'.

checks.item: 1. SAML 2.0: our metadata URL, ACS (HTTP-POST only), IdP metadata pasted or uploaded, the library checks signatures; signed assertion, audience, recipient, NotOnOrAfter, InResponseTo and replay all required
checks.evidence: I read saml.ts and routes-saml.ts. node-saml is set up with wantAssertionsSigned, idpIssuer, audience, ValidateInResponseTo.always, rejectReplayedAssertions and a SQLite cache scoped to the one request id. On top of that, checkAnswer itself checks the bearer Recipient, InResponseTo, NotOnOrAfter, Audience and Issuer. tests/ds-sso-saml-scim.test.ts passes 18/18. In a real browser (Chromium, Playwright, tests/out/verify-ds-sso-saml-scim/browser.cjs and login.cjs, dev server on port 4282 with FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY), a stand-in identity provider page on another site (idp.acme.test) auto-posted a signed answer to /api/sso/saml/acs. The 303 to /finish brought the SameSite=Lax sg_saml cookie back. 'Try a sign-in' landed on /app/settings?tab=security&sso=tried with tested_at set. A new person on a 390 px phone typed the address, pressed Tab (focus moved to 'Continue with Acme sign-in'), then Enter, and ended on /app signed in as sam@acme.test (has_password false). This settles the builder's open question about the Lax cookie, for Chromium only. Safari and Firefox were not tried.
checks.still_broken: When 'Try a sign-in' fails, the admin only sees the generic sso.error.failed text: '{name} did not confirm who you are ... ask the people who run {name}'. The admin is the person who runs it. The real reason (assertion not signed because the provider signs only the Response, wrong audience, wrong recipient, no email attribute) goes only to the server log. A misconfigured provider is the most likely first-day failure, and the admin cannot fix it from the screen.
checks.suggested_fix: In mode 'test' only, pass a short reason code from SamlRefused (unsigned_assertion, audience, recipient, issuer, no_email, expired) to the settings page, with one sentence for each saying what to change at the provider.

checks.item: 2. SCIM 2.0 at /scim/v2: Users create, read, list with userName eq, replace, patch active false, delete; one token per account, shown once and stored hashed; removal goes through the existing removal; 'managed by your directory' stops invitations by hand
checks.evidence: The endpoints work and the tests pass. The token is stored only as SHA-256, a wrong token gets 401 in SCIM form, a cross-account id gets 401, and the owner gets 409. My probe tests/out/verify-ds-sso-saml-scim/probe.test.ts found a privilege escalation. A custom role made with POST /account/roles {base:'admin', left_out:['team']} ('Sid Settings') was refused when removing a full admin by hand: 403 'Your role ... does not include Team'. The same person made a directory token (POST /account/directory/token 200, because the route sits in perm.ts 'settings'), then sent POST /scim/v2/Users {userName:'adam@acme.test', active:false} and got 201. Adam, a full admin, was removed from the team, his work handed over and his keys stopped. Sid could also switch 'Members are managed by your directory' on (200), which then blocked the owner's own invitations (409). removeMember in scim.ts never runs assertMayManage, so 'exactly as an admin removing them does' is not true: the directory can remove anyone except the owner, admins included, on behalf of whoever made the token.
checks.still_broken: Anyone with the 'settings' permission (without 'team') can remove full admins and block invitations through a token they make themselves.
checks.suggested_fix: Put 'POST /account/directory/token', 'DELETE /account/directory/token' and 'PATCH /account/directory' under the 'team' permission in src/server/perm.ts, or require both team and settings. Better: only a built-in owner or admin can make the token. Add a test that a custom role without team gets 403.

repair:ds-sso-saml-scim.notes_for_integrator:
Three ways to abuse the fixes, each handled:
1. A made role makes a token: refused and tested.
2. A made role with Team switches 'managed' or the heir through the API: refused (PATCH also goes through mayRunDirectory) and tested.
3. An attacker reads sso_why: it is only added to an admin's own test-mode redirect, and the codes carry no secrets.

Honest people who could get stuck, each handled:
1. The admin after a failed try: now told the reason.
2. The admin after removing single sign-on: invitations come back, and the card says the directory is paused.
3. Someone with a made admin role: does not see the card. On the Team tab they see only 'Members are managed by your directory ...', without the 'Change this under Settings' pointer.

Left open:
- A token made by a built-in admin keeps working if that admin is later demoted or removed. The token belongs to the account, so a departing IT person does not break the directory. The owner can make a new token or stop it from the card's More.
- When single sign-on is set up again and tried, a 'managed' setting saved earlier comes back by itself and blocks invitations again. This is documented in README and openapi.
- Safari and Firefox are still untested for the SameSite=Lax cookie after the provider's cross-site POST. The reviewers confirmed Chromium only.

done.how: POST /envelopes/:id/offline (src/server/offlinesign.ts prepare, src/server/routes-offline.ts). It needs the sender's or a see_all admin's browser session; API keys are refused. It works only for someone who signs in person and whose turn it is. It uses signView(quiet) so nothing is marked viewed and the account is not locked. It answers the view plus the PDFs as base64, records an audit line and creates the offline_preps table row. Parts that need a connection are refused with the reason: access code, a code we send, group, witness, files to read, attachments, stamps, drawings, fields that depend on other answers. On the device (src/components/sign/offlineInPerson.ts) the copy is AES-GCM under a PBKDF2 SHA-256 key with 600,000 rounds. The PIN must be at least 6 characters and not a run or a repeated digit. Only the dates and the try count are stored in the clear. The dialog (src/components/sender/OfflineReady.tsx) lives in the More of the in-person person on the envelope page. done.item: 3. Online again: sent; accepted only if the envelope did not change since it was prepared (else told plainly); server records when it received it
done.how: POST /sign/:token/offline-finish (public, through the signing link). It checks that prep_id belongs to this recipient and is still in state 'ready', that the copy is at most 7 days old by the server's clock, that the envelope and recipient are open and that content_version is unchanged. Then it records the consent (audit line 'On the host's device without a connection'), claims the prep row atomically and calls completeRecipient with the prep's version. received_at is set equal to completed_at. A refused copy is ended and wiped on the device, with a plain sentence such as 'Nothing was signed for X, because the document was changed after this phone got it ready. Open the envelope with a connection and let X sign it again.' A send that gets no answer, or an answer that is not ours (a Wi-Fi sign-in page), waits. The page sends again by itself every 15 s and on the online event, and offers Send now. A second send is { already: true } and signs nothing twice.

done.item: 5. One envelope per device, 7 days max then the local copy is wiped; not for link signers
done.how: Server: getting a copy ready ends any earlier copy from the same session and any copy for the same person on another device. Each copy expires after 7 days by the server's clock. Device: peek() and unlock() wipe a copy that is too old, by expires_at or by created_at against the device's clock. keep() replaces a copy that holds no result but refuses to throw away an unsent result. The copy is wiped on send, on a final refusal and on Remove. Link signers get 409 not_in_person.

build:ds-offline-inperson.notes_for_integrator:
left_open:
- Words on /in-person are English only; I did not move them into t() or en.json.
- 'I do not want to sign' on the device is not recorded as a decline; nothing is sent, and the README says so.
- Fields are filled in as a form under the pages (with outlines on the pages), not on the pages themselves.
- I verified that the page opens with no signal only in reasoning and in the sw.js code. The dev server registers no service worker, so I did not run a production build to check it.
- A PIN guards against someone who finds the phone, not against someone who copies the browser's storage and tries PINs at leisure (PBKDF2 slows that). The README says so.
- An unsent signature is wiped with the copy after 7 days. The waiting screen says to send it within 7 days.
- Date-signed fields use the day the server received it, not the device day. The certificate says why.

Attacks handled by tests: a made-up prep_id; replay after cancel, expiry, being replaced, or a void; a forged or nonsense device clock; an API key preparing; another account preparing; double send.

Honest-person cases: a changed document gets a plain refusal; a forgotten PIN means getting it ready again, and five wrong tries wipe the copy; a captive Wi-Fi page counts as no answer and the result is kept.

Shared-file edits are one or two lines each: db.ts, pdf.ts, openapi.ts, perm.ts, route.ts, helpers.ts, Recipients.tsx, AppShell.tsx, help/phone.tsx.
